v.verdict: The detail pane now shrinks to its content with a lime top bar and the right side no longer looks like an empty stretched panel, but the volume rows are still mixed into the raid list, the value column is still centred, and the whole screen is still a flat, generic list.

findings.where: middle list, from 'master volume' to 'footsteps volume' (y 710-990)
findings.what: The audio rows still sit under the 'the raid' tab, after an unlabelled gap and a hairline. The audio tab exists in the left column, so the same settings appear to live in two places, and the list is 20 rows long with no group names.
findings.fix: Move the volume rows under the 'audio' tab. If groups have to share a tab, add a 16px tx-2 group label with 24px of space above it, and keep about 9 rows of 56px per screen.

findings.what: About 580px under the pane is empty and the pane is only 290px tall, so the right third of the screen is dead. A 10px hint line stays above it. There is no preview, no list of the value choices, and no default marker.
findings.fix: Use the space under the card for the value choices as a stacked list with the current one marked in lime, or a 'default: off' line at 16px tx-2. Otherwise narrow the pane to 480px and centre it vertically.

findings.what: The values and arrows are centred in a 300px band, far from the setting names at x 354. The eye has to cross about 350px of nothing on each row. The idle arrows are dim, and 'open' has no arrows, so it looks like a different kind of control.
findings.fix: Right-align the value group to x about 1020 with 24px between arrow and value, or pull it to x 560-860. Use tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better for idle arrows, and give 'open' a bordered chip with a '›' marker.

findings.where: left tab column, 'the raid' and 'send play data'
findings.what: The selected tab carries a lime edge and a raised fill while the list row also carries lime, so there are two lime markers at once and the eye splits. 'send play data' floats after a large unexplained gap.
findings.fix: When focus is in the list, dim the selected tab to tx-1 with a 2px edge in --ui-line-hi. Put a 1px --ui-line divider and 24px of space above 'send play data'.

findings.what: The thumb is 8px wide and touches the panel border. The scrolled part has no bottom fade, so the last row, 'footsteps volume', is cut flat against the footer line, and you cannot tell more rows follow.
findings.fix: Make the thumb 6px in --ui-line-hi with a 4px gap from the border, and add a 32px bottom fade to --ui-panel on the list.

findings.where: detail card, 'key: left of 1' chip and description
findings.what: The card uses 4 type styles, and the 'off' value in 56px grey is the only large element but is dim (tx-2 on dark) while the title is brighter. The chip is a bordered button-looking box that cannot be pressed, and the description sits 12px from it.
findings.fix: Make the hero 'off' tx-1, or lime when the value is on. Turn the key chip into plain 16px tx-2 text with no border, and use 24px between the description and the key line.

findings.where: footer 'esc close' and header rule (y 100 and 995)
findings.what: The footer legend is 14px and tx-2, and only shows close; it gives no hint for the pad (change value, back), and the rule at y 995 is closer to the list than the list is to the header. The top-left lime fragment at x 28-60 of the card border looks like a rendering error.
findings.fix: Add 'a change  b back' next to close at 16px. Match the header and footer spacing at 16px. Remove the stray lime tick, or make it a full 3px top bar across the card.

v.verdict: The screen is clean and consistent: card, x, tabs and one lime action are all in place. It is still a small centred form in a huge empty card, with a weak headline and a primary button that does nothing yet.

findings.where: headline '0 runs, 0 notes ready to send'
findings.what: The counts are not the hero. The whole line is the same 32px weight, so the numbers do not stand out and nothing says the state is empty. The previous advice was not followed.
findings.fix: Set the numbers at 56px f-cond 800 in tx-1 and the labels 'runs' and 'notes' at 16px tx-2 under or beside them. When both counts are 0, dim the line to tx-2.

findings.what: The lime primary action is lit even though there is nothing to send (0 runs, 0 notes). Lime then no longer means 'the one useful action', and 'show data' sits right next to it with a tight 8px gap.
findings.fix: When the counts are 0, disable copy to clipboard and show data: use the --ui-raised fill, tx-2 text, no lime. Set the gap between buttons to 16px.

findings.what: The content column is centred at about 1100px under a title and tabs aligned to the 48px margin, so the left edges do not line up. Below the restore panel, about 400px of the card is empty.
findings.fix: Align the column's left edge to x=48, or cap the card at about 1200px for this tab. Fill the height with a status block (last send time, run count) or shrink the card to fit its content.

findings.what: The amber sentence 'paste a restore code, replaces your save.' is a full sentence on screen. It is amber and bold at 16px and competes with the panel title. The panel has the same fill as the card, so it reads as a box with no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Cut it to the tag 'replaces your save' in --warn at 16px, on the title row at the right. Make the title 20px tx-1. Use --ui-raised fill with 24px padding.

findings.where: pil1... input and read code button
findings.what: The input is 54px tall and 1050px wide, while 'read code' is a small button below it, left-aligned and squeezed 16px under the input. The placeholder is dim. The input has no focus border.
findings.fix: Put 'read code' to the right of the input as a 56px-tall button, with the input at 56px height. Set the placeholder to --tx-2. Give the focused input a 2px --acc border.

findings.what: The danger button sits far to the right of the safe actions with 600px of empty space between, so it looks detached. Red outline plus red text at 16px is loud next to the quiet buttons.
findings.fix: Move it into a danger zone below the restore panel, separated by a 1px --ui-line divider, or keep it on the row but dim the border to --danger at 60% until focused.

findings.what: The inactive tab 'game' is a dim grey, a little low in contrast. There is a stray lime tick at the card's top-left corner (x 27-60, y 25). The tabs are 16px, far smaller than the 32px title next to them.
findings.fix: Set the inactive tab to --tx-2 (#aaa498) at 20px f-cond 600. Remove the stray lime tick or turn it into a full-width 2px card top border.

findings.what: The footer legend is tiny and sits at the bottom right with a full-width divider above it. There is no pad button hint, although the screen is meant to be played from a couch.
findings.fix: Show 'b back' in the same footer on pad at 16px tx-2. Keep 'esc close' for keyboard use. Make both 16px minimum.

v.verdict: The party card is now a 90% window as asked, but almost all of it is empty. The content is either pushed to the left edge or floats in the middle of a blank card, and the scrollbar on the input and the explaining sentence are both still there.

findings.what: A 1720x970 card holds one 55px row and two small text lines, so about 90% of it is dead black. Shot 1 shows the content floating at mid-height with a title stranded at y=455. Shot 2 shows it crammed into the top-left strip. The 'make it 90% wide' advice was applied literally to a one-question dialog and made it worse.
findings.fix: Go back to a compact fixed card of about 960x400, centred, and write this exception into the style guide for one-question dialogs. If it must stay large, add a real party panel: four 96px slot rows (p1 to p4, empty slots in tx-2) with the host/join actions in a right column.

findings.where: layout consistency between the two shots
findings.what: The two screenshots disagree. In shot 1 the title sits mid-card at y=455 and the body is indented 431px, so the title, divider and controls don't share a left edge. Shot 2 is flush left at 119px. The card is vertically unanchored, with a 400px gap above the title in shot 1.
findings.fix: Pin the header row at the top (56px high, title 32px/700 at left padding 32px, x in the same row). Use one left edge of 32px for the title, status and controls. Never vertically centre the content block inside a full-screen card.

findings.what: The scrollbar thumb is still visible inside the input, so it is still a textarea or overflow:scroll. The field is 630px wide, which is much too wide for a short code. The 16px placeholder is dim and the focus state can't be seen.
findings.fix: Use a single-line input with overflow:hidden and resize:none. Make it 320px wide, 56px high, with a --ui-line-hi border. Give it a 2px --acc border on focus. Set the placeholder to tx-2 at 16px with a 6-char mask format.

findings.where: title block and body copy, left
findings.what: The 'up to four pillagers, one invite code.' sentence is still there. It is an explaining sentence, so it is a clutter defect. The title is about 30px and the two 15px grey lines below it are barely readable, and the gap between them is uneven (35px).
findings.fix: Delete the sentence. Keep one 16px tx-1 status line, 'not in a party', with '0/4' right-aligned in the same row. Title 32px/700. Body text must not go below the 16px label floor.

findings.what: 'host a party' (200px, lime fill), the input (630px) and 'join a party' (200px) sit in one run with 14-16px gaps. They look like one form row, so the two actions are not separated. Join is always active even when the field is empty, and the lime fill is the only focus-ready element, so pad focus is unclear.
findings.fix: Put host on its own row at the left (240x56, lime). Below it add a 'join with code' group: input 320px + join 160px, with join greyed out until the field has text. Use a 32px gap between the groups. Show a 2px --acc focus ring plus a 4px inset bar on whichever control has pad focus.

findings.where: toast overlapping the card bottom edge, y=1004-1041
findings.what: The 'the welcome pack is in your stash.' toast straddles the card's bottom border, cutting the 1px line through its box. It looks like a stray overlap, and the toast uses a different, smaller 15px style from the rest.
findings.fix: Move the toast inside the safe area, 48px above the bottom edge of the screen (below the card), or inside the card with 32px padding. Give it --ui-raised fill and an 8px gap from any border.

findings.what: The 48px x has a full 1px outline in its idle state. It is heavier than the title and sits at 16px from the corner, but the title padding is 21px, so the two aren't aligned.
findings.fix: Make the x 40px with a borderless idle state and the outline only on focus. Use the same 32px inset from the top and right edges as the title uses on the left, so the header row lines up.

findings.what: The card is flat #121416 with a thin border, with no depth against the scrim. Nothing says 'party' beyond the word itself. The card feels like a generic modal.
findings.fix: Add a 3px --acc bar at the left of the title row or a small party glyph. Use --ui-panel fill, --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Put 4 empty player slots on the card so the screen looks like this game.

v.verdict: Only the OLD screenshot (img-2780-1.jpg) was supplied and there is no NEW image to compare, so this scores the old backpack panel, which reads as a flat dark box with weak hierarchy and a lot of tiny same-weight text.

findings.what: No NEW screenshot was provided, so no comparison could be made.
findings.fix: Resend the NEW 23-raid-backpack-open-1080 image; until then the old-vs-new verdict stays n/a.

findings.what: The card has no accent, no x close in the corner and a thin 1px border. It is not the 90% centred card with a corner x that the owner ordered. The only close cue is the faint 'b or i to close' text at the top right, so it reads as a debug popup over the map rather than a window.
findings.fix: Add a 32px x button at the top right, set the panel to --ui-panel #16191b with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, and keep the close hint at 16px tx-2.

findings.where: equipped block, 'scav pistol' row and stat lines
findings.what: The hierarchy is flat. The title 'backpack' (about 20px), the item name 'scav pistol' and the stats all sit at about the same size and weight. The stat lines ('dmg 23 range 42m semi mag 12', 'integrity 100/100 armour 0 backpack 4 belt 1') are tiny, with no separation between label and value. The pistol icon is about 40px and overlaps the 'dmg' text.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px/700. Set the item name to 20px/600 tx-1. Set stat labels to 16px tx-2 and values to 16px tx-1 in aligned columns with 24px gaps. Move the stats at least 8px below the icon row so nothing touches it.

findings.what: The tiles are small (about 84px) and sit in a huge empty area, so the backpack looks nearly empty. The focused tile has a lime border and is the only strong colour on the card, which is correct, but the tile has no name, no rarity bar and no value on it. The 2 and green-bar markers are cryptic.
findings.fix: Make the tiles 96px with an 8px gap, add a 3px rarity bar on the bottom edge, put the count at 16px bottom-right, and use the free space for a 6-column slot grid showing empty slots.

findings.where: detail section, 'armour plate' / 'use armor' / hint line
findings.what: The detail pane is sparse and badly aligned. 'use' and 'armor' float with a large gap, there is no real button for the action, and the hint line 'arrows move z drop one drag to tactical belt' is an unseparated string of tiny text that reads as a sentence. The price '$340 each' is right-aligned at the same weight as everything else.
findings.fix: Put the detail on a --ui-raised #1e2225 pane. Make 'use' a lime filled button (--acc, text --acc-ink, 20px, 40px tall) with a key chip. Split the hints into key chips at 16px in a footer row with a 1px divider, and make the price tx-1 16px.

findings.where: HUD behind the card (top-right panels, extraction tag, concealed tag)
findings.what: The raid HUD is competing with the card. The scrim is missing, so the map and the run info panel stay at full brightness, and small yellow, teal and amber tags (extraction c available, concealed · in cover) pull the eye. 'extraction c available' has an odd arrow glyph.
findings.fix: Add a --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) layer, or at least 60%, behind the card, and dim the HUD to 40% while the backpack is open.

findings.where: bottom hotbar and prompt 'scav pistol fire use'
findings.what: The hotbar slot 1 (amber) and slot 4 (blue) highlights clash with the lime focus. The 'fire' key chip is white-on-dark and unlike the other chips. Slot digits are about 12px, below the 16px minimum.
findings.fix: Use one focus colour (lime) for the selected slot, make slot digits 16px, and use one key-chip style (1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px) everywhere.

findings.what: The hp bar is a bright green fill with 'hp 100' at about 32px in a soft white font, and the stamina bar is a pale blue, so the two bars use different tints and the hp text is bigger than the title of the open window.
findings.fix: Use --ok for the hp fill only, make both labels 16px/600, and make the bars 8px tall with the number on the right.

v.verdict: Only the OLD screenshot (23-raid-backpack-open-1080) was supplied and no NEW image was attached, so I could not compare. As the OLD screen stands it is a 2: a small, mostly empty dark box with tiny tiles and clipped, crowded text, floating above the hotbar with no card chrome or X.

findings.what: The NEW version was not provided, so no before/after judgement is possible. All findings below describe the OLD screen and may or may not still apply.
findings.fix: Re-send the NEW 23-raid-backpack-open-1080 capture alongside the OLD one.

findings.what: The three item tiles are about 84px and sit in a roughly 830x470 panel with a large dead band below them. The backpack is the point of the screen but reads as three small icons. The selected tile's lime border is the only strong accent, and nothing else shows what is in the bag. Hierarchy is flat: title, weapon name and item name are all about the same weight.
findings.fix: Make it a proper grid with 96-112px tiles and 8px gaps, with rarity bars on every tile and empty slots drawn. Give the detail pane --ui-raised. Make the selected item name 32px title and the rest 20px or 16px, so one thing leads.

findings.what: The window does not follow the settled card rule: it has no X in the corner, no 56px header row and is not a centred, near-full-screen card. It floats with a hard flat edge that sits 30px above the hotbar and covers the lower map. Closing is a text hint, 'b or i to close', in tiny grey type at the top right.
findings.fix: Use the shared card: centred at 90% width and height, 4px radius, --scrim .80 behind it, an x button 40px at the top right, and the title at 32px f-cond 700. Drop the 'b or i to close' text, or move it to a 14px footer legend.

findings.where: weapon block, 'dmg 23 range 42m semi mag 12' and the stat lines below (y≈590-640)
findings.what: The stat line is crammed under the weapon icon, and the icon's ammo pip overlaps the 'd' of 'dmg'. The two stat rows are run-together strings of the same grey with no label or value separation, about 15px. The 'integrity' and 'armour 0' / 'backpack 4' / 'belt 1' row is unrelated data mashed into one line.
findings.fix: Put the stats in a 2-column label/value grid, 16px f-cond with tx-2 labels and tx-1 values, 24px under the icon row. Move the icon pip inside the 48px tile. Give integrity a bar, not text.

findings.where: hud styles: 'standing', 'stamina', 'hp 100' and the top-right info boxes vs the backpack panel
findings.what: There are three type voices: a pixel-ish font in the hp, stamina and standing HUD, a thin condensed font in the top-right cash panel, and a bolder Barlow-style font in the backpack. The guide bans pixel type. The HUD boxes also use mismatched fills and borders, and the run info text is about 14px, under the 16px minimum.
findings.fix: Set every HUD and panel string to Barlow Condensed 600 at 16/20px, with 800 only for the hero hp number at 56px. Use the --ui-panel fill and a 1px --ui-line-hi border on all of them.

findings.what: The 'use' / 'armor' row has a big gap between the two words, with no clear label/value relationship. The hint row 'arrows move z drop one drag to tactical belt' is an explaining sentence in tiny grey. 'armour' is spelled two ways ('armour 0' above and 'armor' here). The price '$340 each' is dim at the far right.
findings.fix: Make it one button-like row: a 'use' action with key chip. Move the key hints to a 14px footer legend with chips, e.g. [z] drop [arrows] move. Pick one spelling. Put the price in tx-1 at 20px.

findings.where: hotbar plus 'scav pistol fire use' prompt chip (y≈930-1060)
findings.what: The prompt chip 'scav pistol / fire / use' is jammed against the panel bottom edge and uses a different chip style (a lighter 'fire' pill). Slots 3, 5-9 are dimmed ghost weapons that compete with the empty bag, and slot 4 has a blue border while slot 1 has an amber one, with no stated meaning.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 35% and hide the ghost icons. Keep a single focus colour (--acc). Hold 16px (--sp-2) clearance between the panel and the hotbar prompt, or hide the prompt while the bag is open.

findings.where: left toasts 'codex entry' and 'contract item nearby', and the 'running slowly' tag
findings.what: Several floating pills with different borders (white, amber, black pill) show over the map with the backpack open. They add clutter and use different shapes, and 'running slowly' sits mid-map as a loose pill.
findings.fix: Use one toast style: 4px radius, --ui-panel fill, 3px left bar in a status colour, 16px text. Suppress non-urgent toasts while a window is open.

v.verdict: The controls list now sits mid-bottom left and folds to a small 'f1 controls' chip, as the owner ordered. But the unfolded panel is a dense, tiny, dim, ragged four-column block that overlaps the log and sits on the water. The HUD around it is crowded and its type sizes don't follow the five-size scale.

findings.what: The key and action text is about 13-14px, and the action column is dim grey on a translucent dark fill over busy water and wall art. That is below the 16px minimum and the 4.5:1 floor for anything read. The four columns (key, action, key, action) have no dividers, no header and no grouping, so the eye has no entry point. Rows are 17px apart, which is cramped.
findings.fix: Raise to 16px f-cond 600 with 24px row pitch. Use tx-1 for keys and tx-2 #aaa498 for actions. Use an opaque --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Group into move / combat / items with a 16px gap between groups, and add a 'controls' label at the top left.

findings.where: image 2, panel position against the left log and the hotbar
findings.what: The panel's left edge (x 493) sits right of the log lines (ending near x 316) with only a ~170px gap, and it floats with no shared baseline against the log or the hotbar. Its top is at y 702, level with the 'codex entry' row, so the two read as one jumbled cluster. It also ends at x 900 and crowds the hotbar tag 'scav pistol / fire / use' at y 940.
findings.fix: Anchor the panel's bottom-left to the same 5% margin as the hp bar (x 24). Put it above the hotbar tag with a 16px gap, and move the log up or stack it above the panel so no rows share a y-band.

findings.what: The contract wraps badly: 'search 2 containers in the' breaks and its continuation 'long dock or scrap line 0/2' is indented, with the count stranded on the second line. The contracts list is also the most prominent and busiest block on screen, with no weight difference between header, label and value, so it outcompetes the new controls. The HUD stack is too dense and runs to six or more text sizes. This is existing clutter, but it makes the new panel hard to find.
findings.fix: Truncate or widen the card to 360px so each contract fits on one line. Make the headers 'contracts' and 'run goals' 16px tx-2 and the rows 20px tx-1. Right-align the counts in a column and drop 'dawn clear' from the card.

findings.what: The folded state is a dim 16px chip lost in the blue water, at the far-left of the bottom area, with 'f1' not set apart from 'controls' by weight or colour. It does satisfy 'folded to one short line', but it is easy to miss and its fill looks different from the neighbouring chips (the 'concealed' and 'standing' tags).
findings.fix: Use the same chip style as 'standing': --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius. Set 'f1' as a key cap in tx-1 and 'controls' in tx-2. Align its left edge to x 24 so it stacks above 'standing', or keep it centred-left at a fixed margin.

findings.what: The panel's '^' caret is about 10px, with no hit area and no label. It duplicates the 'f1 full list' footer at y 854, which is tiny and dim, and the on-screen text is thin as an explanation. The user cannot tell whether f1 or the caret closes the panel.
findings.fix: Remove the caret. Keep one footer hint, 'f1 hide', at 16px tx-2, right-aligned in the panel's footer row.

findings.where: image 1 and 2, left log rows (x 16-316, y 700-800)
findings.what: Log rows use three styles: amber-bar 'contract item nearby', white-bar 'codex entry' and 'stronghold', and no accent on 'golden enemy'. Rows are different widths with ragged right edges, and the amber text is bright warn on a near-black chip. The same alert also appears as 'contract item nearby' in the centre banner, which the owner allows, but the two copies are styled differently.
findings.fix: Give every log row the same 28px height and 4px radius, with a 3px left bar coloured by type (warn, tx-2, danger). Set all text in tx-1 and keep colour on the bar alone.

findings.what: Two stacked banners ('running slowly' and 'contract item nearby · gold glow marks the box') use different fills, text sizes and widths, and they sit under the extract chip. The second line is an explaining sentence, which is a defect under the style rules. It is ~17px type over the map.
findings.fix: Cut the explanation to 'contract item nearby'. Use one banner style at 20px f-cond 600 on --ui-panel, and centre-stack the banners with an 8px gap.

findings.where: image 1 and 2, top-left and top-right cards
findings.what: The 'current pillager bots' card and the cash/stash card use different headers, row heights and value alignments. Each has a tiny ^ toggle in a different place, and the money values wrap around uneven gaps ('cash $900 xp 0'). This breaks one-card-style consistency across the HUD.
findings.fix: Use one card component: 16px tx-2 header, 20px rows on a 24px pitch, 8px padding, values right-aligned in a tabular column, and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Place the toggle at the same top-right offset in each.

v.verdict: The backpack now has a real 8x2 slot grid, so it reads as an inventory and not a loose list, but the card is still an undersized, headerless text stack with no close button, no rarity bars and no key-cap hints.

findings.where: stat rows, selected-item block and hint line (y 480-515, 830-870)
findings.what: The stats are still run-on text ('dmg 23 range 42m semi mag 12', 'integrity 100/100 armour 0 backpack 4 belt 1') with no label/value split. The hint line 'arrows move z drop one drag to tactical belt' is plain text with no key-caps, and sits on the same line weight as the stats. 'use / armor' is a stray two-word row with a big gap, and 'armour' and 'armor' still appear together.
findings.fix: Put stats in a 4-column row with 24px gutters: label 16px tx-2 above value 20px tx-1. Draw the hints as key-cap chips (16px, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px gaps) in a footer row at 14-16px. Use one spelling, 'armour'. Make 'use' a real button: a lime-filled 'use' with a 'e' key-cap.

findings.what: The card still has no X in the corner. The close hint 'b or i to close' is small grey text, which breaks the windows rule. It is about 45% of the width and sits flush against the hotbar (bottom edge 921 against hotbar top 950), so it looks like a popup and not a 90% window. The world behind is barely dimmed.
findings.fix: Add a 32px X button 16px from the top-right corner, with a 'b' key-cap chip beside it. Dim the world behind with --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80). Either grow the card to 70% of the width with 24px padding, or move it to a 90% centred card. Keep at least 24px clear of the hotbar.

findings.what: The slots are empty dark squares at almost the same value as the card, so they are barely visible. Items have no 3px rarity bar. There is no capacity shown in the grid (the '12 / 24' sits up in the equipped row, so it reads as ammo). Only three of 16 slots are used, so the grid feels sparse.
findings.fix: Give each slot a --ui-bg fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Add a 3px rarity bar along the bottom edge of each item. Move the capacity into the header as '3 / 16' at 16px tx-2, and label the '12 / 24' as ammo or remove it.

findings.what: The selected item's name is about 28px bold and is now the strongest element, bigger than the 'backpack' title (about 22px). The title is weak, and the item name and the equipped name are different sizes. The eye goes to the lower name first, and there is no hero element.
findings.fix: Set the title 'backpack' to 32px f-cond 700. Set both item names to 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Add an 8px-padded --ui-raised detail pane around the selected item, with its price in tx-2 at 16px.

findings.what: The weapon icon is a tiny 40px thumbnail with a stray white pip beside it overlapping the 'dmg' text. The weapon has no panel, so it floats between the title and the grid. The 'equipped' label is faint.
findings.fix: Put the equipped weapon in its own --ui-raised panel with a 64px icon, 16px padding, and the 3px rarity bar. Remove the stray pip, or position it clear of the stats text. Raise the label to 16px tx-2 at 600 weight.

findings.what: Spacing is uneven. Title to 'equipped' is about 48px, the grid to the item block is about 55px, and the gap from the item name to its stats is only 8px. The dividers are 1px and barely visible. The bottom of the card has 50px of dead space under the hint line.
findings.fix: Use an 8px grid: 24px between sections, 1px --ui-line-hi dividers, 24px padding at the card bottom. Keep the items close together (8px) within each section.

findings.what: The stat lines are 16px grey condensed text with a pixel-like rendering, thin against the near-black card. At couch distance they are hard to read, and the numbers have no emphasis.
findings.fix: Raise the stat values to 20px tx-1 and keep the labels at 16px tx-2 (#aaa498). Check the contrast is at least 4.5:1.

v.verdict: The only change is a slightly bigger 'backpack' title; the card, stat rows, slot grid, hint line and missing close button are all as before, so it is still a dark default inventory box rather than a polished screen.

findings.where: stat rows, selected item block and hint line (y 480-515, 790-870)
findings.what: The stats are still loose runs of 16px text with no label/value split. 'armour 0' and 'armor' now sit on screen together. 'use' is plain text where it should be a button. The hints 'arrows move / z drop one / drag to tactical belt' are an explaining sentence with no key-caps. The key hints and the 'b or i to close' text are also small and low contrast.
findings.fix: Put the stats in a 4-column grid with 24px gutters: label 16px tx-2 above value 20px tx-1. Use 'armour' everywhere. Make 'use' a lime-filled button with an 'e' key-cap chip. Draw hints as key-cap chips (1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px gaps) in a 16px footer row, and cut 'drag to tactical belt'.

findings.what: No X button, so the close is still the text 'b or i to close'. The world is barely dimmed behind the card, so the HUD and map compete with it. The card is only 45% of the width, and its bottom edge sits about 30px above the hotbar. The 'scav pistol fire use' tooltip is jammed against the card edge.
findings.fix: Add a 32px X button 16px from the top-right corner with a 'b' key-cap chip, and delete the text hint. Put --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card. Grow the card to a 90% centred card, or keep at least 24px clear of the hotbar and the tooltip.

findings.what: The 16 slots are near-identical dark boxes with no border and no rarity bar. The selected lime ring is the only focus cue, and the three items have only a hairline rarity underline. '12 / 24' is an unlabelled number floating at the top right. Capacity isn't shown anywhere.
findings.fix: Give each slot a --ui-bg fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Add a 3px rarity bar along the bottom of each item. Put '3 / 16' in the header at 16px tx-2. Label '12 / 24' as ammo, or remove it.

findings.what: The title is now bigger, but the 'armour plate' item name (about 28px) is nearly as large as the title and sits in a detail zone with no panel. The eye lands on the lime-ringed slot and then on 'armour plate'. The two item names differ in size (pistol 20px, plate 28px).
findings.fix: Make the title 32px f-cond 700 and both item names 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Put the selected item in a --ui-raised pane with 16px padding, with its price at 16px tx-2. Then the title is the only bold element.

findings.what: The pistol icon is tiny, with a stray white pip overlapping the 'dmg' text at about (577,476). The block is not in a panel, and 'equipped' is a dim 16px label.
findings.fix: Put the equipped weapon in a --ui-raised panel with a 64px icon, 16px padding and a 3px rarity bar. Remove the pip or place it clear of the text. Set the label to 16px tx-2 at weight 600.

findings.where: HUD behind the card (top-right run info, left log, bottom-left bars)
findings.what: The HUD stays fully lit behind the modal. Its contract text is brighter than the card's body text, and the amber 'contract item nearby' and teal 'extraction c available' tags pull the eye away. The card's grey text is also the dimmest on screen.
findings.fix: While the backpack is open, dim the HUD to 40% opacity or cover it with the scrim. Raise the card's body text to tx-1 at 20px.

findings.what: The card is a flat black rectangle with a hairline divider and no accent bar, header rule or tab structure. It could belong to any game.
findings.fix: Add a header row 56px high with a 1px --ui-line rule beneath it. Add a 4px lime tick beside the title. Use consistent 24px padding so the card reads as the same family as the shop and codex cards.

v.verdict: The question card is now a real modal with a lime yes button, an outlined no button and a neutral border, but it is still a floating box over a fully lit HUD, with a dead title row and an unlabeled countdown.

findings.what: The 80% scrim from the previous review is still missing. The run info panel, controls panel, hotbar and ammo block all compete with the card at full brightness. Because the card's own border is gone, the card now reads weaker against the busy map than the old teal-bordered box did.
findings.fix: Add a full-screen rgba(6,7,8,.80) scrim under the card. Alternatively, hide the controls panel and run info panel while the question is open. The card should be the only bright element.

findings.what: The 16-line key list is still open under the modal. It is a dense table of mixed-weight text in two columns, and its raw 'ctrl / c' and 'lmb' rows are noisy. It was already flagged and is unchanged.
findings.fix: Hide it while the card is open. Outside the card, fold it to one 16px line ('f1 controls'), per the owner's ruling that it starts folded.

findings.where: card border and edges, x 587-1333, y 262-515
findings.what: The card has no visible 1px --ui-line-hi border, and no shadow separates it from the map. Its dark fill bleeds into the dark window edges at the left and bottom. A stray 55px lime tick on the top-left edge looks like a bug. It is probably a countdown bar, but with the bar's track missing it reads as an artifact.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius. Make the countdown a full-width 3px bar with a --ui-line track and a lime fill that drains. Remove the orphan tick.

findings.what: The title is about 28px and cream-coloured. Its left edge matches the yes button's left edge, which is correct, but the row beside it holds a lone '12' at about 18px in the far right corner. The number has no label or unit and no visual link to the buttons. The title row also has about 80px of dead space above it, and the 32px gap to the buttons is uneven.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px tx-1 f-cond 700 and make it the only bold line. Replace '12' with 'auto no in 12s' at 16px tx-2, or with the draining bar. Use 32px top padding and 24px between the title and the buttons.

findings.what: The lime yes button is a big flat 325px slab with a 20px black label, and the no button is a hairline ghost with a faint border. The contrast between them is correct, but the focus state is unclear. A pad player cannot tell whether yes is the focused button or just the primary style. The key caps 'y' and 'n' are plain text, not key caps.
findings.fix: Put 'y' and 'n' in 1px-bordered 4px-radius key caps inside each button. Give the focused button a 2px --acc-hover outer ring. Raise the no border to --ui-line-hi and use tx-1 for its text. Show the pad glyph (a / b) when a pad is in use.

findings.what: This is unchanged and still carries the earlier findings. The pixel face is still used for 'run info' and the goal lines. The values are ragged and not right-aligned ('+300 sp', '+200 sp', '+400 sp' end at different x positions). The header is only 16px, and the body type is about 17px.
findings.fix: Use Barlow Condensed 600 at 20px. Right-align the +sp values in tabular numerals. Give the panel 24px padding and a 16px tx-2 header. The pending cw-trcol work covers the layout, so leave the corner position alone.

findings.what: The 'team score' label is about 13px, below the 14px floor and in thin pixel type. The 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' lines are tiny and sit awkwardly beside the 36px '0 sp'. The block hugs the top edge with no padding.
findings.fix: Set the label and the you/p2 lines to 16px tx-2. Add 16px top padding. Keep only the hero number at 56px, with the '9:00' timer in a clear second tier.

findings.where: hud corner stack (bottom left, bottom right)
findings.what: The hp bar is saturated green and stamina is saturated blue, with the pixel face on both. 'standing' sits in a notched tag unlike every other panel. The ammo panel and hotbar use different border and radius treatments. The corner type reads as a leftover pixel-font dialect.
findings.fix: Use one 4px radius and --ui-panel fill for all of them. Use Barlow Condensed for the labels. Reserve --ok for hp, and use a muted tx-2 fill for stamina.

v.verdict: The card no longer overlaps the controls legend. It now sits cleanly above the scene with a lime focus letter, a left-aligned title and a corner countdown, but it is still a plain dark box with no scrim, and the HUD stays at full brightness around it.

findings.where: scene behind the card and HUD (whole screen)
findings.what: There is still no scrim. The top-right run goals, the left controls legend, the weapon bar and the ammo block all compete with the modal at full brightness. A modal over a live HUD reads as a debug box, not a AAA moment.
findings.fix: Draw a full-screen rgba(6,7,8,.80) layer behind the card, or at minimum dim the HUD to 40% while it is open. Hide the controls legend (x 492-902, y 702-872) while the card is open.

findings.what: The card is a flat, near-black rectangle with square corners and no border. Only a tiny lime tick sits at the top-left (x 556-610, y 261). It blends into the dark scene and has no frame or depth, so it looks unfinished next to the rounded, bordered HUD panels.
findings.fix: Use a --ui-panel #16191b fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi #4a5257 border and a 4px radius. Make the lime tick a full 3px top bar across the card or remove it.

findings.what: The hint is a run-on of 5 clauses ('type or ▲▼ · space next · backspace back · enter done') at about 16px in a muted colour. It is explaining text, and it is too dense for a couch. The ▲▼ glyphs are bare.
findings.fix: Cut it to two short key hints, 'enter done' and 'backspace back', as tx-2 16px labels. Give the keys small pill glyphs. Centre it 24px under the letter underlines (y 452).

findings.what: The title is left-aligned while the letters and hint are centred, so the card has two alignment axes. The title is also one long line mixing the name and the instruction. The countdown '20' at the top right is tiny and unlabelled, so it reads as a stray number.
findings.fix: Centre the title block. Use 'tonight's best' at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1, with 'enter initials' on its own line at 16px tx-2. Render the countdown as a 32px --acc number or a thin progress bar along the card's bottom edge.

findings.what: The letters are about 48px with thin underlines, and the focus is shown only by lime colour on 'b'. Spacing is loose, with about 100px between letter centres, and the area beneath is empty. The letters feel small for the hero input, and the focus state is thin.
findings.fix: Set the letters to 56px f-cond 800 and use 24px gaps. Give the active slot a 64x72 --ui-raised tile with a 3px lime underline, and keep the idle underlines at --ui-line-hi.

findings.what: The card is 808x294 with about 70px of dead space above the letters and below the title, and the content is sparse. It sits high, close to the extraction pill and the top-centre score.
findings.fix: Shrink it to about 600x280 with 32px padding. Centre it on screen, or 16px lower than centre.

v.verdict: The only change is that the title now reads 'p1 press a' in amber, and the card still mixes a pad-lost prompt with a full pause menu, so most of the earlier advice was not followed.

findings.what: The title still reads as a pad prompt on top of a pause menu, so the card has two jobs. The new amber P1 tint is a per-player colour the style guide says to leave alone until the owner answers r3-13. It also puts warn amber next to the lime resume button, and the guide says never to put those two side by side. The title is still 32px, so the prompt is not the hero element.
findings.fix: Remove the amber tint and set the title in --tx-1. Either title the card 'paused' with 'p1 press a' as a 16px --tx-2 line under it, or show a pad-lost card with a 56px hero 'press a' and no menu buttons.

findings.what: The background is flat near-black with no raid frame and no scrim, so the screen does not read as a pause over a live game. The card is small, about 480px wide in the middle of an empty 1920px screen, and the area around it is dead space.
findings.fix: Show the dimmed raid frame behind the card at rgba(6,7,8,.80). Add the run timer and sector as 16px --tx-2 text. Widen the card to about 560px.

findings.what: There are six buttons in five rows, and the rows are not uniform: feedback and what's new share a row at half width. Report a problem and feedback overlap in purpose. Five equal-weight options is clutter for a pause card.
findings.fix: Keep resume, settings and end run. Merge report a problem and feedback into one 'feedback' button. Move what's new into settings. Use full-width rows 56px high with 16px gaps.

findings.what: The red outline is the same weight as the neutral buttons and sits 16px under feedback, so a mis-press ends the run with no confirmation.
findings.fix: Add a 24px extra gap above end run and a confirm step. Keep the 1px --danger border and add the 3px lime focus bar when it is focused.

findings.what: Focus is shown only by the filled lime on resume. Only one button ever shows focus, so with a pad the player cannot tell focus from the primary action when focus moves to another button.
findings.fix: Give a focused button a 2px lime border, a 3px left bar and the --ui-raised fill. Keep the filled lime for the one primary action. Add a 14px footer legend with the pad glyphs, for example a for select and b for back.

findings.what: A stray 36px olive tick sits on the card's top-left edge, and the x close is a thin glyph in the corner that is not much larger than the title's cap height. Neither does anything useful.
findings.fix: Delete the tick or make it a 3px full-width lime top bar. Make the x a 40px target with a 1px --ui-line-hi border.

v.verdict: The only change is an amber 'p1' prefix on the title, which makes it a little clearer who is in control. Every other earlier P0/P1 problem is still there: the card floats on a flat black screen, the title is still cryptic, and the six-button stack is untouched.

findings.what: The title is still a prompt, not a name. The new amber 'p1' is a second colour in the title. It is set in the old warn amber, and with P1/P2 colours still undecided it adds a per-player tint nobody approved. It also sits next to the lime resume fill and reads as a clash.
findings.fix: Set the whole title in --tx-1 at 32px/700. Title the card 'paused' and put 'p1 press a' on a 16px --tx-2 line under it. Or show a pad-lost card with a 56px hero 'press a' and no menu buttons.

findings.what: The card sits on empty #0b0c0d with no dimmed raid frame behind it. It reads as a dead screen and not a pause over a live game. The 480px card is small, with about 700px of black on each side.
findings.fix: Render the frozen raid frame behind a rgba(6,7,8,.80) scrim. Widen the card to about 560px. Add the run timer and sector as 16px --tx-2 text under the title.

findings.where: button stack (resume, settings, report a problem, feedback, what's new, end run)
findings.what: Six buttons in three different layouts: full-width rows, a 2-up split row and a red outlined row. 'report a problem' and 'feedback' do nearly the same job. The mixed layout makes the menu feel cluttered.
findings.fix: Keep resume, settings and end run. Merge report a problem and feedback into one 'feedback' button. Move what's new into settings. Use full-width rows 56px high with 16px gaps.

findings.what: The destructive action sits 16px under feedback with the same spacing as the safe buttons. One stray press could end the run. It has no confirm step.
findings.fix: Add a 24px extra gap above end run. Add a confirm step. Keep the 1px --danger border and add the 3px lime focus bar when it is focused.

findings.what: Only resume looks focused, as a flat lime fill. The other buttons have no visible hover or focus treatment, so the focus bar the guide asks for is missing. There is no pad legend such as a for select or b for back.
findings.fix: Give a focused button a 2px lime border, a 3px left bar and the --ui-raised fill. Keep the filled lime for the one primary action. Add a 14px footer legend with the pad glyphs.

findings.what: A stray 36px dim lime tick sits on the top edge of the card at x=720–756. It looks like a rendering glitch next to the otherwise plain 1px border.
findings.fix: Remove it, or extend it into a full 3px lime top bar across the card width as a deliberate identity mark.

findings.what: The x is 28px with a faint stroke, and it sits slightly lower than the title baseline. The title row has 16px of space above and 24px below the divider.
findings.fix: Centre the x on the title's vertical midpoint. Give it a 40px hit box and --tx-1 at 70%. Make the spacing above and below the divider equal at 24px.

v.verdict: The card is cleaner and its hierarchy is clear, with one lime resume button, a quiet stack, a red end run and a corner x. The title still reads as a pad prompt rather than a pause, and the card is small and floats on a flat black void.

findings.what: The title is the player-prompt string, not a screen name. 'p1' is amber and 'press a' is tx-1, so two colours compete in a 32px title. The card also does not say what it is (paused). The close x suggests a pause menu, but 'press a' suggests a pad-lost card, so the purpose is unclear.
findings.fix: Title it 'paused' in --tx-1 at 32px/700. Put 'p1 press a' on a 16px line under the title: 'p1' in amber, 'press a' in --tx-2. If it is a pad-lost card, drop the menu buttons and show a 56px hero 'press a'.

findings.what: The card sits on flat #0b0c0d with nothing behind it, so there is no sense of a paused raid. The card is about 480x485 on a 1920x1080 frame, which is small next to the settled 90% card rule and leaves large dead areas.
findings.fix: Render the frozen raid frame under a rgba(6,7,8,.80) scrim. If a 90% card is not wanted for a pause, widen it to about 560px and keep it centred.

findings.what: The stack has too many peers: report a problem, feedback and what's new are all low-value. Row 4 splits into two half-width buttons while the others are full width, so the grid is inconsistent. Report a problem and feedback do nearly the same job.
findings.fix: Keep resume, settings, feedback and end run. Merge report a problem into feedback and move what's new into settings. Use four full-width rows, each 56px high, with 16px gaps.

findings.what: End run has the same 16px gap as every other row, so a destructive action sits right next to feedback. Its red 14-16px text on #16191b is only about 4:1. No confirm step is shown.
findings.fix: Add 24px of extra space above end run. Brighten the text to about #ff6a4f, or use tx-1 on a --danger 1px border. Add a confirm step.

findings.where: top-left of card edge at about x=720..756, y=298
findings.what: A short dim olive accent stub sits on the card's top-left corner. It looks like a clipped or unfinished bar, is not aligned to the title text at x=760, and is not in the style guide.
findings.fix: Remove it, or make it a deliberate 3px x 40px --acc bar inset 0 from the card edge and aligned with the content at x=760.

findings.what: Labels on the outlined buttons are about 18px bold. The guide body size is 20px, and the buttons are 56px high. The idle borders are faint against the panel, so the unfocused rows are weak. A focused state other than the filled resume is not visible.
findings.fix: Set labels to 20px f-cond 600. Set the idle border to --ui-line-hi #4a5257. The focused row gets a 2px lime border plus a 3px left bar and the --ui-raised fill, and resume keeps the fill only when it has focus.

findings.what: The x is about 26px and thin, in the muted tone. It sits about 24px above the title baseline and is not centred on the title line. There is no pad hint for the close action (b).
findings.fix: Centre the x vertically on the title line with a 40x40 hit area. Add a 14px footer legend such as 'b back' at the bottom of the card, in tx-2.

v.verdict: Only the OLD screenshot was supplied, so I could not review the NEW version or compare the two; as a standalone read, this raid HUD is readable but inconsistent and cluttered, a 2.

findings.what: No NEW image was provided (only img-27500-1, the 116-before shot), so no before/after judgement is possible.
findings.fix: Resend the NEW screenshot of the arcade-drop controls card at 1080. Until then 'better_than_before' stays n/a.

findings.where: f1 controls chip, left edge at y≈405
findings.what: The folded controls line sits mid-left, not mid-bottom left as the owner ruled (rs-1). It is a small chip with 20px text and a 1px dark outline, and it floats between the red barrels and the log. Nothing shows that F1 opens a list.
findings.fix: Anchor it at bottom-left, about 32px from the left edge and 24px above the hp bar stack. Match the panel fill #16191b, 4px radius and 1px #4a5257 border. Set the key 'f1' in a --ui-raised keycap so it reads as a key.

findings.where: HUD panel language (score tab, run info, ammo box, hotbar, pills, log row)
findings.what: Five different container looks sit together: a square-cornered tab hanging from the top edge, a rounded black run-info box with a chevron, an ammo panel with a clipped corner and a lime tick, a hotbar tray with 4px slots, and fully rounded pills. Fills and borders vary too. This reads as template parts, not one system.
findings.fix: Use one panel: #16191b at about 88% opacity, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Use it for the score, run info, ammo, hotbar tray and log. Drop the cut corner and make the pills 4px radius.

findings.what: The 'standing' box is a bordered outline unlike every other element. Armour, stamina and hp are three bars at different heights with the label crammed inside. The hp bar is the loudest thing on the left, and the saturated blue and green fills clash with the lime accent. Stamina has no value.
findings.fix: Use one bar height (16px) with 8px gaps. Put labels and values at 16px f-cond above or beside the bars. Show hp in tx-1 at 32px with a thin bar under it. Tint armour and stamina with desaturated tokens, not stock blue and green. Drop the 'standing' box or merge it into the same panel.

findings.what: The score tab, 'extract 108m' pill, 'running slowly' pill and the weather line stack into one 4-row column about 280px tall in the centre of the view. The 'score' label is about 14px. 'running slowly' is a loud white-on-black pill for a minor status. The weather text also appears in the left log, which the owner allows, but here it is a second grey bar sitting on the wall art.
findings.fix: Keep score and timer in the tab. Move 'extract 108m' into the tab as a 16px teal line. Turn 'running slowly' into a small 16px tx-2 status near the vitals. Give the centre notice the shared panel fill so it does not fade into the wall.

findings.what: Nine slots show faint ghost icons on empty ones, and number labels of about 14px at low contrast. Two slots are highlighted: slot 2 in green and slot 4 in amber. Their meanings are unclear, and the amber outline sits close to the lime accent. The 'fire use' hint tags above the bar are tiny and ride on the burst carbine label.
findings.fix: Show only filled slots at full strength and hide empty ones, or dim them to 30%. Give the active slot a 2px --acc border and the secondary a plain line. Use 16px numbers in tx-2 and move the key hints into the footer legend.

findings.what: This is the strongest hierarchy on screen: 24 at about 72px with '/ 144' beside it. But '/ 144' is nearly as heavy as the hero number, and the weapon name is right-aligned at about 30px, competing with the title role. The lime tick on top is unexplained.
findings.fix: Set 24 at 56px weight 800 in tx-1. Set '/ 144' at 20px in tx-2. Set 'burst carbine' at 20px in tx-2. Remove the tick or make it a real reload bar.

findings.what: The goals list is 20px white with uneven indents, and the '+400 sp' rewards sit in the same weight as the goal names. It is a boxed panel, not the vertical 1 by 1 list the owner wants, though he asked screen tasks to leave that corner alone. The chevron is tiny.
findings.fix: Leave the corner alone for now. Make the title 16px tx-2 and the goals 20px tx-1. Right-align the rewards in tx-2 on one column and give the rows 8px gaps.

v.verdict: No NEW screenshot was supplied (only the OLD image exists, and it is the only file in the folder), so I could not compare; this score and these findings are for the OLD raid HUD, which is a 2 because it has several competing boxes, mixed type sizes and the top-right panel is unfinished.

findings.what: The panel is a dense block of 5 sizes of text. Its goal rows run flush to the right edge and the border, and 'run goals' is the same size and colour as 'run info' so there is no hierarchy. The panel sits on top of the building art, which makes it look noisy, and the chevron is tiny. Goal rewards are tx-1 and the same weight as the goal names.
findings.fix: Use the list pattern from the guide: title 20px/700 tx-1, a 1px --ui-line divider, rows at 16px/600 tx-2 with the '+500 sp' on a right-aligned tx-1 column. Give it 16px padding on every side and a 4px radius on --ui-panel at .85 alpha so it does not blend into the map.

findings.what: The hero element is the right idea but all three lines are roughly the same weight and the 'extract 141m' teal pill is a separate box with a different width and left edge. The score is about 36px, not the 56px hero, and the timer is nearly the same size as the score so it is unclear which comes first. The panel is squared off and its edges are cut by the building behind it.
findings.fix: Make '0 sp' the hero at 56px/800 tx-1, the timer at 20px/600 tx-2 beneath it, and put 'extract 141m' inside the same 8px-padded panel as a 16px --extract line. Use one panel width (about 240px), centred.

findings.where: bottom-left status stack (standing / armour 60 / stamina / hp 100)
findings.what: There are four elements in four different forms: 'standing' is a loose grey tag, armour and stamina are thin blue bars of two different heights and widths, and hp is a taller green bar with a larger number. Text sizes vary from 16 to 32px without any pattern. The bars are not on a panel and sit on the map edge with no padding, with the left edge at 22px against the screen margin of about 5%. The stamina bar's text is hard to read against its blue fill.
findings.fix: Put them in one 4px-radius --ui-panel, 16px padding, one column on a 320px width. Use hp at 20px/700 on the largest bar (16px tall) and armour and stamina at 8px tall with 16px labels in tx-2 on the left, not inside the fill. Move 'standing' into the same panel as a 16px state label.

findings.where: bottom-centre weapon bar and prompt strip (riot scattergun / fire / use)
findings.what: The ten slots are all the same size and the empty slots are as bright as the filled ones, so the two usable weapons (5 and 6) do not stand out. The prompt strip above the bar ('riot scattergun, fire, use') is a separate tiny pill with a mixed layout that touches the player's 'shield' label and the bar top. The purple slot 5 has an 'f' label that looks like an artifact. Slot numbers are 14px and low contrast.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 40% and give the active slot a 2px --acc border only. Move the prompt to a 16px line centred 16px above the bar with a 16px gap from the player's label, and bump slot numbers to 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The '7 / 42' is a good hero, but the card is a different shape and fill from the other panels, has a faint yellow line on top that reads as a rendering glitch, and the weapon name is at 28px, the same weight as the number's neighbour. The right and bottom edges run into the screen edge, with no margin.
findings.fix: Use the common panel (--ui-panel, 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi), margin 5%, weapon name at 20px tx-2, and ammo at 56px/800 with the '/ 42' at 20px tx-2.

findings.where: left log (fog, stronghold, golden enemy) and 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: Rows use three different left treatments (bar only, info icon, nothing), widths follow the text and the semi-transparent backgrounds make them hard to read against green foliage. 'f1 controls' floats at mid-left with no relation to other elements. Per the owner's ruling the controls hint should be mid-bottom left in career raids.
findings.fix: Use one row template, 16px/600 tx-2, a 3px left bar in the alert colour, fixed 280px width, and an 80% --scrim fill. Move 'f1 controls' to the bottom-left above the status stack as a 16px key chip.

findings.what: Every corner has a differently shaped box (square, rounded, no box, a lined card), so the HUD reads as a pile of unrelated widgets and not as a system. Corner margins differ from 0 to 22px, and several panels are clipped at the screen edge.
findings.fix: Apply one panel style and one 48px margin (5%) from the edges to all five HUD groups.

v.verdict: Only the OLD image (img-14924-1.jpg) was supplied and the NEW image path is missing, so no comparison is possible; this is my read of the OLD raid HUD, which is cluttered and inconsistent.

findings.what: The NEW screenshot was not provided. I could not check what changed or whether it is better. The findings below describe the OLD version only.
findings.fix: Supply the NEW image path, for example img-14924-2.jpg, and re-run the review.

findings.where: top centre alert banner plus the log rows at bottom left
findings.what: The red 'overseer sweep laser' banner is about 400px wide with a 40px glyph and a 36px title. It is the loudest element on screen and pushes the score and extract readout down to second place. The same alert also sits in the left log, which the owner has ruled stays. So the banner is the only part that can be calmed.
findings.fix: Cut the banner title to 32px. Use a 4px danger-red left bar on --ui-panel with no red fill. Cut the glyph to 24px. Keep the score as the only 56px hero element.

findings.where: 'pillager reinforcements' pill under the banner and the log rows at bottom left
findings.what: A black pill under the banner is a third style of toast. The log rows use a fourth style, with a left bar, an info icon and mixed text opacity. Panel fills, radii and bar treatments differ. The pill has square corners and a pure-black fill rather than --ui-panel. The pill, the banner and the log therefore look like three different systems.
findings.fix: Use one alert component: --ui-panel fill, 4px radius, a 3px left bar coloured by severity (danger, warn, tx-2), 20px text, 8px padding. Apply it to the banner, the pill and the log rows.

findings.what: The panel is about 300px wide with 18-20px text, and nothing sets its title apart from its content. 'run info' and 'run goals' are both title-like and both near white. The three goal lines run together, with the 'sp' rewards in the same weight and colour as the goal names. It is a dense block of 16px-equivalent text with a chevron that is hard to see. It also sits in the corner the owner will rebuild as a vertical 1 by 1 list (key cw-trcol), so only small fixes belong here.
findings.fix: Make the title 16px tx-2 and the goals 20px tx-1. Put the rewards in tx-2 and right-align them in a column. Add a 1px --ui-line divider. Leave the corner layout for cw-trcol.

findings.where: bottom-left status stack (standing, armour, stamina, hp)
findings.what: Four different treatments are stacked with no common rhythm. 'standing' is a grey box, armour and stamina are thin blue pills, and hp is a thick, bright green bar with a 32px label. The bars have different heights and label placement, and the stamina bar is dim. Only hp should be strong. Armour reads as cyan and blends with the extract teal, which is reserved for extraction only. Blue and green fills are also far from the palette's single hot accent.
findings.fix: Use one bar component: 12px high, 4px radius, a --ui-line track, tx-1 labels at 16px. Fill hp in --ok and make it the only strong bar, 20px with a 32px number. Fill armour in tx-2 and stamina in --ui-line-hi. Do not use blue or teal.

findings.where: weapon hotbar at bottom centre and the ammo block at bottom right
findings.what: The hotbar is a row of nine equal dark slots with faint numerals and ghosted icons. The two filled slots are tiny and the ammo count '360' is about 14px, below the 16px floor. The selected slot has an amber border, but lime is meant for selected, so this is off-palette. The ammo block uses a 56px-class '60' next to a '/ 360' of the same weight, so the hierarchy inside it is weak. The 'support mg' label above the hotbar and the 'fire / use' key chips sit loose on top of it with uneven padding.
findings.fix: Draw the selected slot with a 2px --acc border and --ui-raised fill. Make all slot ammo text 16px. Set '/ 360' in tx-2 weight 400 beside the 56px '60'. Align the 'support mg' label and key chips to the slot row's left edge, 8px above it.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' chip and the rain tag at left
findings.what: The 'f1 controls' chip sits mid-left, floating against the screen edge at about x=10, in a different box style from every other element. The owner's ruling puts it mid-bottom on the left, folded to one line. The 'rain' tag in the log has a different opacity again, so the status lines have no consistent rule.
findings.fix: Move the chip to the mid-bottom left and use the shared panel style at 16px. Make 'rain' use the same log row component at the same opacity as the other rows.

findings.where: score and timer block, top centre
findings.what: The score '0 sp' and the timer '9:45' are both bold at the same size, so they compete. The extract chip below sits in a separate sliver with a different fill and slightly misaligned edges. The block hangs from the top edge with a tab-like shape that nothing else on screen shares.
findings.fix: Make the score the one 56px hero with the timer at 32px. Fold the extract line into the same panel as a 16px --extract text row, so it is one block with one outline.

v.verdict: The HUD is unchanged from the last review: the vitals, run info panel, ammo block and top-centre score card still each use their own styling, and the screen is cluttered with stacked toasts and tags.

findings.what: The bars are still three different thicknesses, with the hp bar much taller than armour and stamina. The labels use different sizes and weights, and 'hp 100' at about 32px outshouts everything. The armour blue and stamina teal are nearly identical, and the 'standing' pill is a boxed 28px label that competes with the bars.
findings.fix: Make all three bars 12px high with 8px gaps and a 16px f-cond label inside the left edge. Use --ok for hp, tx-2 for stamina and one cool blue for armour. Turn 'standing' into a 16px tx-2 tag 8px above the stack with no box.

findings.what: The panel has no border, radius or fill token and sits 4px from the screen edge with no 5% margin. The title and 'run goals' are close in size, with no clear tier between them, and the chevron is tiny. The goal rows have no 32px pitch and the rewards aren't right-aligned. It crowds the 'meridian strongbox' label directly below.
findings.fix: Use panel P: #16191b at 90%, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding, and inset it 48px from the edge. Set the title at 20px 700 tx-1 and 'run goals' at 16px tx-2. Use a 32px row pitch with rewards right-aligned in tx-2. Make the chevron 24px and leave 16px below the panel before any world label.

findings.where: Top-centre score card, extract line and toasts (880-1160, 0-262)
findings.what: The card is glued to the top edge with no offset. The extract pill, the teal arrow, the 'running slowly' toast and the storm toast are stacked in one column and read as four separate pieces. The arrow floats loose in the world. The 'storm' toast uses a third pill style with faint text, and its contrast over the busy map is poor.
findings.fix: Offset the card 24px from the top. Make 9:58 the 56px hero with 'sp' as a 20px tx-2 line. Put the extract line inside the card as a 16px teal row. Move the arrow to a screen-edge indicator. Put toasts 72px below in one pill style (4px radius, 3px left bar, 16px text, 90% opaque panel) and show only one at a time.

findings.what: The panel has a hard-edged chamfer and a lime sliver at the top, which no other panel uses. The weapon name sits right-aligned at 28px, the hero '60' is much bigger than 56px, and '/ 360' sits unevenly beside it. The panel is only about 10px from the screen edge, which does not match the vitals' margin.
findings.fix: Use the shared panel P with a 4px radius and 16px padding. Set the weapon name at 20px tx-2, '60' at 56px 800 tx-1 and '/ 360' at 20px tx-2 on the same baseline. Inset 48px from the corner so it lines up with the vitals and run info panel.

findings.what: The hotbar is the heaviest element on screen. All nine slots carry the same weight, and the empty slots are dark greys that fade into the map. The ammo count text inside the slots (about 14px) is below the 16px floor. The 'support mg / fire / use' prompt above is cramped against the bar, with a lone key cap that doesn't match the 'f1' hint.
findings.fix: Use 56px slots with 8px gaps, tx-2 numerals at 16px minimum, and a lime border on the selected slot only. Dim empty slots to 50% with no icon. Put the prompt 16px above the bar with one key-cap style shared with 'f1'.

findings.what: The hint is a floating box with no key cap and flat text. The 'storm' tag has a different left bar and padding, and the two sit at different edge offsets. In this shot the hint is also mid-screen at 386px, not top-left or mid-bottom-left as the settled raid-controls ruling says.
findings.fix: Draw 'f1' as a 28px key cap with a 16px tx-2 'controls' beside it. Use one pill style for this hint, the storm tag and the toasts, with a 4px radius, 3px left bar, 16px text and the same 48px edge inset. Place the hint at mid-bottom left per the ruling.

findings.what: The orange label sits in a gap under the run info panel with no backing, and its colour is close to the warn amber and the rarity gold. It reads against the beige floor poorly.
findings.fix: Use a 16px tx-1 label on a 4px-radius panel backing, with a small --r-gold 3px bar as the only accent. Keep it at least 16px clear of the run info panel.

findings.what: The new screenshot's map differs from the old one, but every HUD block is unchanged. Each block is a different dark box with its own edge offset, radius and type size, which is the template tell the guide forbids. Nothing from the last review was applied.
findings.fix: Build one panel P and one pill style, apply them to every HUD block, and snap all corner insets to 48px on the 8px grid.

v.verdict: The how-to-play panel and the old B / I backpack clutter are gone, which is a real cleanup, but the HUD is otherwise unchanged: the status stack, score block, run goals and ammo panel are still small, uneven and generic, and the move-to-start prompt is still only a tiny 'shield' tag under the player.

findings.where: Player 'shield' tag (960,600) and hotbar prompt strip (burst carbine / fire / use)
findings.what: This screen is the move-to-start state, but nothing tells the player to move. The only cue is a 14px teal 'shield' word under the feet, and the fire/use strip is a third, separate prompt. The first thing the eye hits is the pink/purple building tint, not the action.
findings.fix: Add one centred prompt at about y=62% in 32px f-cond 700 tx-1, e.g. 'move to start', with a 56px-high key cap for wasd (or the pad stick) on a --ui-panel 90% chip with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Drop the 'shield' label to 16px tx-2 or remove it. Fold fire/use into the hotbar footer legend at 14px.

findings.where: Bottom-left stack: 'standing' chip, armour 60, stamina, hp 100 (24-1050)
findings.what: Bars have inconsistent treatment. Armour and stamina are thin (about 22px) and blue, with labels crammed inside. HP is a heavier green bar with a larger label, and the 'standing' chip floats above with a different border and size. The stack sits about 24px from the edge, not the 5% margin, so it crowds the corner. On this frame the world label 'the forge' is clipped behind the hp bar.
findings.fix: One bar component: 320px wide, 16px high, 8px gap, 16px tx-1 label above each bar in f-cond 600. HP is the only exception: bar 24px high, with a 32px number. Make 'standing' a 16px chip aligned to the same left edge. Inset the stack 48px from the left and bottom, and keep world labels out of the HUD zone.

findings.what: The block is welded to the top edge with no top padding. The 'score' label (14px) is far smaller than the 56px 'sp' number. The extract chip is a separate teal box stuck on the bottom edge with a 2px mismatch in width, and the arrow overlaps the chip. Three stacked sizes with no shared container look improvised.
findings.fix: One 280x112 --ui-panel 90% card, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 24px from the top. Inside: sp number at 56px f-cond 800 tx-1, timer at 20px tx-1 beside it or below, and the extract line at 16px --extract inside the same card, with the arrow 8px to the right. Remove the 'score' label or set it to 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The panel is flush against the right and bottom edges with no inset, so it fights the hotbar for the same baseline. The weapon name is right-aligned in tx-2 and the hero ammo number is right-aligned, but a ghost weapon icon at left is almost invisible. The yellow tick on the top edge is an unexplained 50px accent mark. The reserve '/ 144' is nearly as large as the hero number.
findings.fix: Inset the panel 48px from the right and bottom. Hero '24' at 56px f-cond 800 tx-1, reserve '/ 144' at 20px tx-2 on the same baseline. Weapon name 20px tx-2 left-aligned, with the weapon icon at 100% opacity beside it. Use the lime tick only to mark the selected slot, or remove it.

findings.what: This is a flat text block with a dim 'run goals' sub-label at the same size as the rows. The chevron is far from the label. The rows are tightly packed (about 26px pitch) and the sp values are not right-aligned, so the numbers don't scan. It is cut off from the top edge by only 65px and from the right edge by 20px, which doesn't match the score block.
findings.fix: Make it one card: 16px tx-2 label 'run goals', rows at 16px tx-1 with a 32px pitch, and sp values right-aligned in --acc-free tx-2 in a tabular column. 16px padding, 1px --ui-line-hi border, --ui-panel 90% fill, 48px from the right edge and 24px from the top to share the score block's top line. Drop the 'run info' header, since the chevron already says it folds.

findings.what: Eight empty slots at about the same weight as the two filled ones read as a wall of dark boxes. The slot numbers are 14px tx-2, the ammo counts inside slots are tiny, and the selected slot (gold outline) and the 'f' marker are the only differentiators. The orange selection outline is gold-like rather than lime, which breaks the 'lime means selected' rule.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 40% opacity and remove their icon silhouettes. Use a 2px --acc outline and a --ui-raised fill on the selected slot. Slot numbers 16px tx-2, ammo count 16px tx-1. Keep the hotbar centred on the same bottom 48px margin as the ammo and status stacks.

findings.where: Left log (fog / stronghold / golden enemy, 20-300, 680-780) and 'f1 controls' chip (10-132, 385-427)
findings.what: The log chips are different widths with 1-2px left bars, and the text is 18px tx-2 at low contrast over the busy terrain, so it is hard to read. 'f1 controls' is a heavier chip with a different corner radius and sits alone at mid-left with no relation to the log.
findings.fix: Use one chip style: --ui-panel 85% fill, 4px radius, 16px tx-1 text, 8px vertical gap, left-aligned to the same 48px inset. Put 'f1 controls' in the same style, at the bottom of the log column or mid-bottom left as the owner ordered.

v.verdict: The new shot is cleaner in one respect: the red alert banner and the two threat rows are gone from the log. But the top-centre pill still duplicates the log's last row, and the score block, run info panel and vitals still have the problems I listed last time.

findings.where: top-centre 'pillager reinforcements' pill and the bottom row of the left log
findings.what: The same event is shown twice, 40px apart in the top-centre pill and again as the log's brightest row. My earlier advice was to show a live alert only in the top card, and the pill still reads as a loose afterthought rather than a card. The owner's rs-2 ruling only protects the red banner plus its log row. This is a pill plus an info row, so the ruling doesn't cover it.
findings.fix: Make the live alert one 320x40 card with a 3px --warn left bar, 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 text, 16px padding, and 16px below the score block. Show the log only for events older than the live alert. Don't repeat the live event as a bright row.

findings.where: left event log (running slowly, stronghold, golden enemy, pillager reinforcements)
findings.what: Four rows are still the max-3 I asked for, and the row widths are ragged (about 130, 280, 180 and 260px). Each row has an info icon, and a '· 1 on the map' tail makes the stronghold row an explaining sentence. The three older rows are dimmed to grey on grey, so they are barely readable over the busy terrain.
findings.fix: Use a max of 3 rows, each a fixed 320x32 --ui-panel at 90% with a 3px left bar (--warn for info). Use 16px f-cond 600 text in tx-1 or tx-2, with an 8px gap between rows. Delete the icons and the '1 on the map' tail. Fade older rows by opacity only, to a floor of 60%.

findings.what: The 'run info' header and chevron are redundant. The goal rows are crammed at 18-20px in one weight, with no divider and about 6px of padding. The rewards are not right-aligned. The panel butts the minimap edge and sits 20px from the screen edge. The first goal row is a goal with no progress count ('air strike +300 sp'), which breaks the pattern of the rows below it. The 'the long dock cache' label is clipped at the right edge.
findings.fix: Drop 'run info' and the chevron. Make 'run goals' a 16px tx-2 label, then 20px tx-1 goal names with the reward right-aligned in tx-2. Use 16px padding, 1px --ui-line dividers, and a 24px margin from the screen edge. Give every goal an n/m count. Keep the dock cache label at least 24px inside the screen.

findings.what: Three stacked fragments make three nested boxes, and the extract pill hangs off the card at a different width. The 9:45 timer is only about 28px, so nothing here reads as the hero. The score at roughly 36px outranks the timer. The cyan arrow floats 20px below the pill, detached from it, and the block is flush against the top edge with 0px margin.
findings.fix: Use one panel 16px from the top. Put the timer in 56px f-cond 800 tx-1, the score as a 20px line beneath it, and the 16px --extract line with the arrow attached to its left. Use one 4px radius and 16px padding.

findings.what: The hp bar is a different height from the other two (about 32px against 22px) and the type sizes differ. The label in the bar is at 20px for hp but 16px for armour and stamina. The damage chip '-5' is a red block jammed against the bar's right end. The 'standing' tab in a grey box floats above with a different fill. Armour blue and stamina blue are almost the same colour, so the two bars are hard to tell apart.
findings.fix: Draw three bars at 20px high with 8px gaps. Put the 16px label inside the left edge and the value on the right. Use --ok for hp, --extract for stamina and a neutral for armour. Make 'standing' a plain 16px tx-2 label with no box. Show the damage as a tx-1 number that fades out.

findings.where: world-space enemy labels (crawler c-54, crawler m-33, sentry t-94)
findings.what: The two crawler labels overlap each other and are unreadable, at 14px orange on orange terrain with no backing. Contrast is low, and the red tint over the scene lowers it further.
findings.fix: Give each label a 4px radius, an 80% --ui-void backing and 16px text. Stack overlapping labels at 20px offsets, or show only the nearest one.

findings.where: 'extraction c available' tag (right) and 'f1 controls' chip (left)
findings.what: The extraction tag is cyan on a dark chip with an arrow glyph that's misaligned with the baseline, and it clips against the screen edge. The 'f1 controls' chip is a different fill and radius from the other chips and floats at mid-left with no anchor.
findings.fix: Use the same chip component as the log rows (32px high, 4px radius, --ui-panel at 90%). Keep a 24px margin from the right edge. Move 'f1 controls' to mid-bottom left, as the owner ruled, folded to one line.

v.verdict: The backpack card still looks like the earlier version: a dark box with loose text rows and plain slots. None of the earlier advice (key-cap hints, close X, slot borders, rarity bars, a raised detail pane) was applied.

findings.where: Card frame (530-1390 x 327-921) and close hint at top right (y 367)
findings.what: The close control is still the text 'b or i to close' in muted grey. It is not an X button. There is no scrim behind the card, so the busy map shows through the dark card. The card is about 45% of the screen width and sits right on top of the hotbar tooltip ('scav pistol fire use', y 940), with only about 20px between them.
findings.fix: Add a 32px X button 16px from the top-right corner with a 'b' key-cap chip, and delete the text. Put --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card. Grow the card to about 90% of the screen, or keep at least 24px between the card and the hotbar.

findings.what: 'armour plate' is shown as a bare title with tiny stat text. 'use' and 'armor' sit on one line with no labels, so they read as unrelated fragments. 'armor' conflicts with 'armour' elsewhere in the card. 'use' is plain text where it should be the primary action. The hint line ('arrows move  z drop one  drag to tactical belt') is a sentence in 16px grey with no key styling, and 'drag to tactical belt' explains the interface in words.
findings.fix: Put the selected item in a --ui-raised pane with 16px padding. Name at 20px f-cond 600 tx-1, price at 16px tx-2. Make 'use' a lime-filled button (--acc, --acc-ink text) with an 'e' key-cap chip. Use 'armour' everywhere. Draw hints as key-cap chips (1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px gaps) in a 16px footer row, and cut 'drag to tactical belt'.

findings.what: Empty slots are nearly invisible dark squares with no border. The filled slots have no rarity bar. The armour plate is selected with a lime frame, but the other two items have only a thin grey or green underline that follows no rule. The grid has no count (such as '3 / 16'), so a player cannot see how full the pack is. Spacing between slots is uneven against the 8px grid.
findings.fix: Give each slot a --ui-bg fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, with an 8px gap. Add a 3px rarity bar along the bottom of each item. Show '3 / 16' in the header at 16px tx-2.
