findings.fix: Make it a 64px-tall button with --acc fill, --acc-ink 32px f-cond 800 text, a 4px radius and 24px side padding. Remove the '!'. Keep it 16px above the pad, clear of the pillars, with a 2px --acc-hover ring when it's in focus.

findings.where: bottom controls strip (wasd walk, shift jog, e use station, m map)
findings.what: The key chips are about 14px, and the labels are tx-2 on a near-black fill. It touches the hotbar 12px below and hides under the stash pad. Four separate chips with uneven gaps crowd the controls and look cluttered.
findings.fix: Set the text to 16px f-cond 600, with label tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Use 24px gaps between pairs and 32px above the hotbar. Draw one --ui-panel strip. Fold it to one line as in the rs-1 rule, with F1 to open.

findings.what: Slot 1 has a gold-ish outline and slot 2 a green fill with a lime bar. Two active-looking slots confuse which one is selected. The dim silhouettes in slots 3 to 9 are close to the panel at about 2:1. The slot numbers are 14px and low-contrast.
findings.fix: Make only the active slot carry a 2px --acc border with --ui-raised fill. Drop the green tint from slot 2 and use a 3px --acc bar for 'equipped' only on the active slot. Raise the silhouettes to tx-2 at 60%. Make the numbers 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The 2 stat lines at about 14px in tx-2 are barely readable at couch distance. The card is inset only about 80px from the left, which doesn't match the right-side margin.
findings.fix: Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 and the stats to 16px f-cond 600 tx-2, with 16px padding. Align the card to the same 48px left margin as the currency card on the right.

findings.what: The big translucent glow circles overlap each other and the crowd of NPCs. A second brownish circle by the mainframe sits unlabelled, and the pad rings are drawn in five different hues. The scene feels noisy next to the HUD.
findings.fix: Draw the glow at 50% of its current opacity. Use one ring colour per station type from the existing tokens. Remove the unlabelled brown circle, or give it a label. Keep the circles from overlapping the labels.

v.verdict: This is a different screen from the last review, the hub with the party's overlapping crowd and the pad of stations. The eye lands on the lime 'enter raid!' sign, which is correct, and the labels are clean, but the top-right currency row is raw, the station labels disagree in style, and the amber warning label is noisy.

findings.what: '$4,471,337', '98,761 xp' and 'stash $0 bag $0' sit as three loose strings with no panel. They differ in size and weight and sit on a busy backdrop. The stash and bag text is dim, small, and low-contrast against the dark void. The row also carries two hero-sized numbers, which competes with the lime enter raid sign.
findings.fix: Put the row in one --ui-panel pill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, anchored at x 1872 (48px margin) and y 24. Make money 32px tx-1 and xp 20px tx-2. Set 'stash $0 bag $0' at 16px tx-2 as a second line, or drop it, because the stash label is already given by the stash station. Keep one hero size on the screen.

findings.what: The amber text is an explaining sentence wrapped in asterisks, and it is the only amber on the screen. It sits stacked on top of the 'the last pour' label, and the asterisks look like debug text. It breaks the clutter rule and the straight-copy rule.
findings.fix: Delete the asterisks and the sentence. Show a 16px --warn 'beta' chip, 4px radius with a 1px --warn border, inside the 'the last pour' label at 8px padding, or drop it altogether.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, the mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash, fashion, the last pour)
findings.what: All labels use the same tag. Their text size is about 18px, so none fall on the 20px body size. Nothing tells the player which one is nearest or in focus, and no pad focus or ring is shown. The 'shop, craft, and hire' label is a sentence-like list, unlike its neighbours. The '6 rewards waiting' chip is much smaller (about 14px), so it fails the 16px floor.
findings.fix: Set station labels to 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Give the nearest station a 2px --acc border and a lime 'e' keycap. Shorten the shop label to 'the shop'. Raise '6 rewards waiting' to 16px and make it a lime-ink badge ('6') on the mainframe label.

findings.what: The sign is the right focal point, but it is a lime 56px headline with an exclamation mark on a black box with no border. It is the only lime fill-like element, and it has no key or button prompt. It sits over the station bubble and the pillar at the top, so it looks pasted on. The player does not know how to trigger it.
findings.fix: Make it a --acc fill button, 4px radius, with --acc-ink 32px text 'enter raid', and add an 'e' keycap on the right. Drop the exclamation mark. Set 8px padding top and bottom. Keep it centred on x 960 and offset it 8px above the station ring.

findings.where: hotbar (x 457-1467, y 953-1062) and the controls hint (x 757-1165, y 900-940)
findings.what: The two blocks nearly touch: the hint's bottom edge is within 14px of the slot tops. The hint text is only about 14px. The empty slots 3 to 0 are still showing full weapon silhouettes, which is clutter in the hub. The selected slot is brown/amber, not lime, so the selection colour is inconsistent with the guide. The slot 2 green fill and the white bar do not follow the rarity 3px rule.
findings.fix: Raise the hint to 16px and move it to y 900 with a 24px gap above the hotbar. Dim slots 3-0 to 30% or hide them in the hub. Make slot 1 a 2px --acc border on a --ui-raised fill. Replace slot 2's fill with a 3px rarity bar at the bottom.

findings.what: The panel's title at about 28px is fine, but its subtitle '0 items in stash · 0 runs' is about 14px, and a middle dot is used as a divider. The card sits at x 81, y 47 instead of the 48px margin. It does not align with the currency strip at the right (y 22-56).
findings.fix: Set the card at x 48, y 24. Set the subtitle to 16px tx-2. Share one baseline with the currency panel at y 24. Use the same panel fill and border.

findings.what: The chip is wedged against the top edge, in green mono-like text at roughly 16px. It is an off-palette teal outline and sits 6px from the screen edge. It is unclear what it communicates.
findings.fix: Move it to y 24 and give it a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and tx-2 text. Alternatively fold it into the controls hint on the bottom as a small 'keyboard' label.

findings.where: the play area frame (x 157-1765) and the character crowd
findings.what: The world frame has hard letterbox bars at left and right. The wall is pale grey-purple, with big translucent station circles overlapping one another, notably the mainframe's second pink bubble (x 1355-1535). A pile of 15 characters sits in the middle with no depth treatment. The result looks busy, and the rings muddy the labels.
findings.fix: Drop the overlapping bubble at x 1355-1535 or reduce its alpha to 8%. Cap station ring fill alpha at 12%. Darken the wall to --ui-bg so the lime sign and the labels read first.

v.verdict: The hub reads clearly and the station labels now share one pill style, but none of the earlier fixes to the currency strip, the experimental tag, the enter-raid title or the controls strip have been made, so it still looks like a prototype, not a polished lobby.

findings.where: top-right currency strip ('$4,471,337  98,761 xp  stash $0 bag $0')
findings.what: The strip is unchanged: two ~32px bold white figures with no panel, a tiny 'xp', and a faded 'stash $0 bag $0' at 14px. It sits on bare floor and wall and runs into the dark window edge. The stash and bag figures are close to unreadable. The money figure competes with 'enter raid!'.
findings.fix: Put it in one --ui-panel card (4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px padding) 48px from the right and 32px from the top. Stack three rows: money at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1, xp at 20px, and 'stash $0 · bag $0' at 16px tx-2 (4.5:1 or better). The card must sit fully inside the playfield.

findings.what: It is still lime display text with an exclamation mark, on a dark box that overlaps the pillars. It is not a button and has no pad focus state. It is the biggest element on screen and also the primary action, yet it looks like a header, not something you press.
findings.fix: Make it a 64px-tall button with --acc fill, --acc-ink 32px f-cond 800 text, a 4px radius and 24px side padding. Drop the '!'. Put it 16px above the pad and clear of the pillars. Add a 2px --acc-hover ring when it has focus.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' above the last pour
findings.what: The asterisks and the amber 14px sentence are still there. It is an explaining sentence, it breaks the clean look, and it is crowded against the 'the last pour' pill so the two read as one stack. It also uses the old amber instead of the --warn token.
findings.fix: Remove the sentence and asterisks. Add a 16px f-cond 600 --warn 'beta' tag with 8px padding on the top-right of the 'the last pour' label.

findings.where: station labels and prompts ('6 rewards waiting', 'the mainframe', 'wirt the gambler', 'the stash', 'fashion', 'shop, craft, and hire', 'settings', 'the last pour')
findings.what: All eight labels are pills of the same weight, so nothing shows which station is nearest or focused. 'shop, craft, and hire' is a clause where the others are nouns. 'wirt the gambler' and 'the mainframe' repeat the article. '6 rewards waiting' is a second pill at a smaller size stacked above its label. Their distance from their pads varies, and 'fashion' sits off-axis from its pad.
findings.fix: Anchor every label 16px above its pad and centred on it. Show the nearest station's label with a 2px --acc border and the others at 70% opacity. Shorten to 'shop', and drop 'the' from 'the stash', 'the gambler' and 'the mainframe'. Render '6 rewards waiting' as a 16px --acc dot-and-number badge on the mainframe label's corner.

findings.what: Large translucent circles in purple, teal, pink, amber and brown overlap one another (the mainframe and settings areas, the stash and centre circle). They add muddy blotches that fight the character art, and they use hues outside the palette. The central brown circle has no label or purpose.
findings.fix: Draw each zone as a 2px --ui-line-hi ring at 40% opacity with no fill. Keep the nearest zone's ring --acc. Remove the central circle or any zone that has no station.

findings.where: bottom controls strip (wasd walk, shift jog, e use station, m map)
findings.what: It is still open as four pairs at about 14px, with low-contrast labels, and it sits pressed against the hotbar (about 12px gap) and overlaps the stash and fashion zones. It ignores the rs-1 rule to be folded and mid-bottom left.
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px f-cond 600 line, 'f1 controls', in a --ui-panel pill at mid-bottom left. F1 opens the full list. Leave a 32px gap above the hotbar.

findings.what: It is the one panel that uses the right idiom (a bordered card with a title), but its 'items in stash · runs' line (about 14px, dim) duplicates the stash figure at top-right. The card's top-left and the currency card's top-right are inconsistent sizes.
findings.fix: Make it 32px f-cond 700 for the title and 16px tx-2 for the meta line. Delete the duplicated stash count from the top-right card. Match its 4px radius, border and 16px padding to the new currency card, with both 32px from the top.

findings.what: Slot 1 has an amber border and slot 2 a green fill, so two different 'selected' looks appear at once. Eight empty slots are shown as dim ghost icons with 14px number labels, which adds noise in a social hub where the weapons cannot be used.
findings.fix: Use one selected state, a 2px --acc border with no fill, on one slot only. Hide the hotbar in the hub, or show only the owned slots, with 16px numbers in tx-2.

v.verdict: The hub is readable, and 'enter raid' is a clear lime focal point. The top-right strip, the beta tag, the plain station labels and the busy hotbar are all unchanged from the last review, and that is what keeps this at 3.

findings.what: This is the same loose row of text as before. Money and xp are bare numbers at the same size, with no panel, and the 'stash $0 bag $0' text is dim and tiny. 'xp' is a stray small label. The row runs to x 1893, past the 48px margin, and has no container.
findings.fix: Put the row in one --ui-panel pill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, anchored at x 1872 and y 24. Make money 32px tx-1 and xp 20px tx-2. Set 'stash $0 bag $0' at 16px tx-2 on a second line, or drop it.

findings.what: The asterisks and the explaining sentence are still there. They are clutter, and the amber text on a dark chip crowds 'the last pour' and the character beside it.
findings.fix: Delete the asterisks and the sentence. Show a 16px --warn 'beta' chip, 4px radius, 1px --warn border, 8px padding, attached to the 'the last pour' label.

findings.what: It reads well, but it is a bare lime-on-black text plate and not a button. It has no 'e' keycap, and the exclamation mark is an arcade tell. The 56px type is also bigger than the title scale allows, and it sits over the pillar edges and the NPC's head.
findings.fix: Make it a --acc fill button with --acc-ink 32px text 'enter raid', 4px radius, 8px vertical padding, and an 'e' keycap on the right. Centre it at x 960 and keep it 8px above the station ring.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, the mainframe, shop craft and hire, settings, the stash, fashion, the last pour)
findings.what: All the labels share one flat dark chip, so the nearest station is not marked and there is no 'e' prompt. '6 rewards waiting' at about 13px is too small to read from a couch. 'shop, craft, and hire' is long for a label.
findings.fix: Set labels at 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Give the nearest station a 2px --acc border and a lime 'e' keycap. Shorten the shop label to 'the shop'. Make '6 rewards waiting' a 16px lime-ink '6' badge on the mainframe label.

findings.where: station glow circles (all stations, plus the large circle at x 800-1125, y 390-710)
findings.what: The translucent discs overlap each other, for example around the mainframe at x 1355-1535. They also muddy the floor and look like stray blobs. The big central disc has no label or purpose.
findings.fix: Cut the disc fill to 8% and draw a 2px ring instead. Show the ring only for the nearest station. Remove the central disc, or move it clear of the other stations so none overlap.

findings.where: hotbar (x 457-1467, y 953-1062) and controls hint (x 757-1165, y 900-940)
findings.what: The hint is 14px and sits tight against the hotbar, only about 13px above it. Slots 3-0 are dimmed but still draw full weapon silhouettes, which adds noise in the hub. Slot 1 has a gold border that reads as warn amber and not the accent.
findings.fix: Raise the hint to 16px and put a 24px gap between it and the hotbar. Cut slots 3-0 to 30% opacity or hide them in the hub. Give slot 1 a 2px --acc border on a --ui-raised fill, and use a 3px rarity bar for slot 2.

findings.what: The title is a good size, but the 14px 'items in stash · runs' line under it is too small and repeats the stash value in the top-right strip. The panel has a different border and padding from every other chip.
findings.fix: Use a 16px tx-2 second line, or fold it into the top-right strip. Match the border and radius to the new 4px --ui-panel style, and align the left edge to the 48px margin (x 48).

findings.what: A small teal chip sits at the top edge, floating alone. Its meaning is unclear, and teal is reserved for extraction only.
findings.fix: Move it into the top-right strip or the controls hint as a 16px tx-2 label with no teal. Align it to the 24px top margin.

v.verdict: The HUD is readable and has a sound hierarchy (ammo, hotbar and timer), but the earlier advice was mostly not followed: the hp bar is still bare, the roster is still open, and slots 3 to 0 still show silhouettes.

findings.what: The bar has no panel, border or track. 'hp 100' is about 32px bold, which is louder than the ammo number, and it sits on the busy map and clips against the bottom edge. This was advised before and not done.
findings.fix: Put it in a 4px-radius --ui-panel card with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Set the bar to 24px high with a --ui-raised track. Use 20px/600 for 'hp 100'. Turn the fill --warn below 50% and --danger below 25%. Keep a 24px margin from the left and bottom edges.

findings.what: The roster is still open and takes up about 360x120px. Dead rows repeat '- dead'. The row text is about 14px with uneven pitch. The bottom line '0 out · 2 dead' duplicates the dead rows. The grey 'pillager' name tag and bar then sit directly under it, so two similar boxes stack up.
findings.fix: Fold it by default to one line, '0 out · 2 dead', with a chevron. When open, use 16px/600 rows on a 24px pitch, show dead rows at 40% opacity, and delete the '- dead' column. Leave a 16px gap before the pillager tag, or move the tag to the hp card.

findings.where: bottom-right ammo card footer 'b / i backpack  3 items $1,220'
findings.what: The footer is about 14px in tx-2 and sits tight against the card edge. The key hint is plain text. '$1,220' has the same weight as '3 items', so the money does not read first.
findings.fix: Use 16px/600 f-cond. Add a 1px --ui-line divider above the line and 16px card padding. Colour '$1,220' tx-1 and keep '3 items' in tx-2. Turn 'b / i' into a key chip like the 'f1' one.

findings.where: hotbar slots 3 to 0 and slot numbers
findings.what: Unowned slots still show dim weapon silhouettes. That adds eight rows of visual noise and makes it unclear what the player owns. The slot numbers are about 12px. The blue border on slot 4 competes with the lime active border on slot 1.
findings.fix: Show only a 16px tx-2 number in empty slots, with no silhouette and a 1px --ui-line border. Reserve the 2px lime border for the active slot. Mark an owned but inactive slot with a --ui-line-hi border and a full-colour icon.

findings.what: The timer has no backing and sits on a busy tree and ground, while the extract chip sits on a teal-bordered dark chip. The two read as separate widgets. The teal arrow floats below the chip with no clear link to it.
findings.fix: Put the timer and the chip on one 80% --scrim plate with 8px padding. Attach the arrow to the plate's bottom edge with a 4px gap, in --extract.

findings.what: The two use different box styles. The keyboard tag has a green border with a lime-green fill, and the contracts box has a dark fill with no visible border. The 'pillager 236m' marker is about 14px and low contrast on the map.
findings.fix: Give both a 1px --ui-line-hi border, --ui-panel fill, 4px radius and 16px/600 text. Give 'pillager 236m' a 2px dark text shadow or a small scrim chip, and use 16px.

findings.what: It floats at about 14px right above the hotbar's left edge, over a pale wall, so its contrast is weak. It is also not aligned to the hotbar.
findings.fix: Put it on a --ui-panel chip at 16px. Left-align it to the hotbar's left edge (x=548) with an 8px gap above the hotbar.

findings.what: The names are about 40px in a grey-on-purple box, which is bigger than every other label on screen and bigger than the hp readout. The thin amber health bars sit on the plate bottom with no frame.
findings.fix: Reduce the names to 20px/600 tx-1 on a --scrim plate. Give the health bar a 6px high --ui-raised track. Keep the amber fill only for elite or armour, and use --danger for hostile health.

v.verdict: This is a raid HUD, not the hub my last review covered, so none of that advice applies. The ammo hero number and hotbar read well. The pillager list is cluttered, the banners are teal and pink in several styles, and the hp bar is oversized and off-grid.

findings.what: 'extraction c avallable' has a typo and no 'c' key or pad-button cue. The 'extract 146m' pill and the 'extraction c available' pill are two separate pills with a stray triangle glyph between them. They repeat the same information, and extract teal is used for both.
findings.fix: Fix the text to 'extraction open' and merge both pills into one pill at 20px f-cond 600: '146m' in tx-1 and a 'c' keycap on the right. Remove the triangle, or use it as a 16px bearing arrow inside the pill. Put the 8:56 clock above it at 32px and leave 8px between them.

findings.what: The panel is crowded and its header is hard to read. 'current pillager bots 0' is a long label with a stray count. Names are muted grey and small, and the dollar amounts are tiny and right-aligned in the same weight as the names. The collapse caret has no obvious meaning. 'you $1,020' also repeats the bag value in the ammo card. The footer '0 out · 3 dead' makes the panel feel like a debug dump.
findings.fix: Shorten the title to 'raiders' at 16px tx-2 with +.04em tracking. Make rows 16px f-cond with 24px height. Show 'you' in tx-1 with an amber (P1) 3px bar on the left. Leave the others in tx-2 with a --danger 'dead' tag. Drop the '0 out · 3 dead' footer, and drop $1,020 from this row if the bag card already shows it. Fill the panel with --ui-panel, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius.

findings.what: The bar is a flat full-green slab that is the loudest element on the screen. 'hp 100' is oversized in a fat glyph that runs into the bar's edge, with no frame. It is not the hero number, so it is competing with the 12 / 24 ammo.
findings.fix: Use a 320x16 bar inside a 1px --ui-line-hi frame at x 48, y 1024, with a --ok fill. Put the 'hp 100' label at 20px tx-1 above the bar, and align it to the hotbar baseline at y 1060. Keep the 56px hero size for ammo only.

findings.what: Free-floating pink text with no panel or icon. It is off-palette, since pink is not a token. It looks like a debug label, and the 'contracts 0/8' dropdown above it is an unrelated style.
findings.fix: If it's a zone label, set it at 20px f-cond 600 in tx-1 on a --scrim pill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, or use --warn if it's a hazard. Anchor it under the contracts dropdown with 8px of gap.

findings.what: It is a wide, dark bar that nearly touches the screen edge, with a chevron and no visible focus or key hint. Its margin is under 24px and it doesn't line up with the left panels at x 8.
findings.fix: Set a 24px margin, so x 1872 and y 24 on the right edge. Use 16px type, 'contracts 0/8', with a 'tab' keycap in place of the chevron, and make the panel narrower, at about 200px.

findings.where: left stack alignment (x 8-367 list, x 14-170 'pillager' bar, x 24-430 hp, x 436-540 'f1 controls')
findings.what: Four left-hand elements start at four different x values (8, 14, 24, 436) with uneven vertical gaps. The 'pillager' name bar floating under the list reads as a leftover.
findings.fix: Align every left element to x 48, with 8px steps vertically. Fold the 'pillager' name bar into the list's own row and remove the separate bar.

findings.what: It is a green-text pill with a mono-weight 'keyboard' label jammed into the corner, in a style used nowhere else on the screen. It is not a clear control hint.
findings.fix: Remove it from the raid HUD, or reduce it to 14px tx-2 with no fill.

findings.what: The hero 12 / 24 works, but the 'b / i backpack' and '6 items $1,020' footer lines at about 14px are cramped against the card edge. The weapon name sits too tight to the right edge.
findings.fix: Use 16px type, 16px padding, and a 1px --ui-line divider above the footer. Show '6 items' in tx-2 and '$1,020' in tx-1.

v.verdict: This is a readable raid HUD with a strong ammo hero number and a clear weapon bar. It sits on an inconsistent margin grid, and the HP and armour bars, the score plate and the goals dropdown each use a different type size and panel treatment.

findings.what: The plate is glued to the top edge with no margin and has square corners. Three type sizes are crowded inside it: 'team score' in 16px, '0 sp' in about 40px, and the small 'you 0 sp / p2 0 sp' lines. The 'extract 135m' chip hangs off the bottom edge as a separate pill. The plate reads as a stack of fragments rather than one card.
findings.fix: Inset the plate 24px from the top. Use a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make '0 sp' the single 56px f-cond 800 hero number and the clock a 20px tx-1 line. Put 'you' and 'p2' on one 16px tx-2 line. Fold the extract line into the plate as a 16px --extract row with 8px padding so no chip overhangs.

findings.what: The bars start 22px from the left edge and 4px from the bottom edge. 'hp 100' is about 32px, much bigger than 'armour 60' at 20px, so the two bars look unrelated. Both are saturated flat fills with the text inside them. The edge margin does not match the ammo card on the right.
findings.fix: Inset the stack 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom, the same as the ammo card. Make both bars 28px tall with 20px f-cond 700 labels. Put them in one --ui-panel card with a 4px radius, 8px gap and 16px padding. Reserve the 56px hero size for the ammo count only.

findings.what: It is a light-bordered box with a chevron. The border, fill and radius match no other HUD panel. It is the only top-right item, so it looks like a leftover web select. Its text is about 24px, a size outside the scale.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a --ui-panel card with a 4px radius, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 20px f-cond 600 text. Pin it 48px from the right and 32px from the top. Align its top edge with the score plate's top edge. Make the chevron 16px tx-2.

findings.where: bottom weapon bar and ammo card
findings.what: The weapon bar is 1000px wide and clear of the ammo card. The slot numbers are about 14px and low contrast against the dark tiles. Empty slots 3 to 0 are near-black and look like dead UI. The selected slot 2 has a lime-yellow border, but slot 1 keeps a blue border that competes with it. The ammo card ends 8px from the right edge, so it does not line up with the 48px margin. The weapon name 'compact smg' is small tx-2 text above the hero '30 / 180'.
findings.fix: Make slot numbers 16px tx-1. Draw only the selected slot with a 2px --acc border and give every other slot a 1px --ui-line-hi border, including slot 1. Dim empty slots to 50% opacity. Move the ammo card to 48px from the right and 32px from the bottom, with its bottom edge level with the weapon bar. Raise the weapon name to 20px tx-1.

findings.what: It is a tiny dark-green chip jammed into the corner with no margin. It carries a device label nobody needs mid-raid. It sits where the player expects the squad or status cluster.
findings.fix: Remove it from the raid HUD, or inset it 32px and 48px with 16px tx-2 text and no fill. Show it only while the controls list is open.

findings.what: The side plate has a thin cyan bar under a name in a different font size from the other HUD text, and it floats at x=17 with no margin. The in-world 'shield' label is clipped by the player sprite and the foliage. It is unreadable at about 14px.
findings.fix: Move the plate to 48px from the left. Set the name at 16px f-cond 600 in --extract (cyan, per the P2 colour rule). Make the bar 6px tall. Draw in-world labels at 16px with a 1px dark outline, 8px above the sprite head and in front of foliage.

findings.what: Its key cap and label sit on a faint dark chip about 12px above the weapon bar. The chip has no border and its edge blurs into the map. The 'f1' cap is not tied to the shared key-hint style. It sits 24px from the weapon bar but is not aligned with the hp stack.
findings.fix: Give it a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius with 8px padding. Use a 16px f-cond 600 label in tx-2. Align its left edge to the 48px margin and its baseline to the top of the weapon bar.

v.verdict: The new frame is cleaner, with the pillager list and the double banners gone, but the top-centre card is crowded, the hp and armour bars are chunky and overlap the bottom edge, and the HUD uses too many different panel styles.

findings.where: top-centre score card (x 810-1112, y 0-107) and extract pill (x 889-1033, y 103-133)
findings.what: The card is jammed against the top edge with no margin. 'team score', a 56px 'sp' hero, a tiny 'you 0 sp / pl 0 sp' and the clock are all stacked in it. The extract pill overlaps its bottom edge, and the teal arrow floats loose below it. The 'you' and 'pl' lines are about 14px and low-contrast.
findings.fix: Give the card a 24px top margin and 16px padding. Put the 56px hero 'sp' and the 32px clock on a single column. Set 'you 0 sp · pl 0 sp' at 16px f-cond in tx-2 on one line, and drop the 'team score' label. Move the extract pill 8px below the card as a separate element, and put the arrow inside it as a 16px glyph.

findings.what: The bars are 30-34px tall solid fills with 36px text. They are the loudest things on screen, louder than the ammo hero, and they butt against the bottom edge. They have no frame, and the armour and hp stack has no gap. The block sits 24px from the left edge while the hotbar starts at x 555.
findings.fix: Use 320x16 bars in a 1px --ui-line-hi frame with a 4px radius, an 8px gap between them and a 48px bottom margin. Put 'hp 100' and 'armour 60' at 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 above or beside the bars. Keep the hp fill --ok and the armour fill a muted blue. Align the block's bottom with the hotbar's bottom at y 1056.

findings.what: Four different containers sit on screen at once: the score card (black, hard-edged), the goals dropdown (dark with a lime-grey border), the ammo card (rounded with a glow border), and the hotbar. Radii, fills and border weights differ, so the HUD reads as a template with no system.
findings.fix: Use one container: --ui-panel at 85% opacity, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and 16px padding. Apply it to the score, goals, ammo and hotbar. Reserve lime for the selected slot only.

findings.what: The dropdown is 300px wide for a two-word label. It sits 17px from the right edge, not 24px, and has a chevron where a key hint would be. It is also at a different height from the score card.
findings.fix: Set the width to about 200px and the right margin to 24px. Align the top with the score card at y 24. Replace the chevron with a 'tab' keycap at 16px. Use 16px type.

findings.what: The hero '60 / 360' is correct, but the card is 8px from the right edge and 62px from the bottom, so it doesn't line up with the hotbar or the hp block. The card's glow border differs from the other panels. 'support mg' at about 28px competes with the hero.
findings.fix: Set the right and bottom margins to 24px/48px. Set 'support mg' at 20px tx-2. Use the standard panel style, and keep 56px for '60' only, with '/ 360' at 32px tx-2.

findings.what: The unselected slots are very dark, so the weapon icons are barely visible. The numbers are about 14px and sit in the corner. The selected lime slot and the blue slot 6 are close in prominence, which blurs focus. The 'f1 controls' tag floats at the left edge of the bar at an odd size.
findings.fix: Raise the idle icon opacity to 60% and set the slot numbers at 16px tx-2. Show the selected slot only with a lime border and an --ui-raised fill. Mark slot 6 with a 3px rarity bar, not a blue fill. Put 'f1 controls' on the panel's baseline at 16px.

findings.where: player 1 tag (x 16-170, y 322-360) and 'keyboard' tag (x 8-105, y 6-32)
findings.what: The player 1 tag at the left edge is a blue plate with no margin and a cyan bar. It's detached from the character, and amber is the P1 colour. The 'keyboard' tag in the corner is a green-on-black chip in a different style from every other panel.
findings.fix: Use --ui-panel with a 3px amber (P1) bar on the left and 16px type in tx-1, and offset it 24px from the edge. Move the 'keyboard' tag into the same chip style at 14px tx-2, or drop it from the raid HUD.

v.verdict: The hub reads as a game, with a clear lime 'enter raid!' call and tidy station labels, but the top-right currency line, the amber warning tag and the heavy circular glows crowd the scene and break the style guide's type and token rules.

findings.where: top-right currency line ('$4,471,337  98,761 xp  stash $0 bag $0')
findings.what: Three different sizes and weights run together with no panel. 'stash $0 bag $0' is dim grey on the dark side band and nearly unreadable. 'xp' is tiny and floats. The line sits on the scene with no plate, and the 98,761 figure is not clearly a separate stat from the $ figure. It also repeats the stash count shown top-left.
findings.fix: Put it in one --ui-panel card (4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border) pinned 48px from the right and 32px from the top. Show '$4,471,337' at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 and '98,761 xp' at 16px tx-2 beneath it. Remove 'stash $0 bag $0' from here, since the top-left card already has the stash count. Never use text dimmer than the 4.5:1 tx-2.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' tag under 'the last pour'
findings.what: It is a long amber string with decorative asterisks, a different tag style from every other station label, and the tightest text on screen. It reads as a debug note and is explaining-sentence clutter. It also nearly touches the label above it.
findings.fix: Replace it with a 16px --warn 'experimental' chip, 4px radius, 8px padding, 8px under the station name, with no asterisks. Or drop it and put the warning inside the bar window.

findings.where: proximity glow circles (every station, plus the large grey circle at the centre and the bottom-left)
findings.what: The big translucent discs overlap in places: the mainframe disc has a second pink disc on top of it, and the stash disc runs into the fashion disc. They muddy the dark floor, fight the character sprites, and two of them (centre grey, bottom-left) have no station label, so they read as stray artefacts. Each station tints a different colour, which weakens the rule that lime alone means 'selected'.
findings.fix: Cut the disc fill to about 8% opacity and give it a 1px ring in the station colour. Remove the unlabelled grey and pink discs. Keep one ring colour per station and use lime only on the station the player is nearest to.

findings.what: Slot 1 has a 2px gold-amber border and slot 2 a green fill, so two slots look selected. Eight of the nine slots hold dark grey weapon icons that are barely visible, so the bar is mostly empty and heavy. The slot numbers are about 12px and low contrast. The bar sits tight against the controls strip above it, with about 12px of gap.
findings.fix: Draw only the active slot with a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill. Give the rest a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 50% opacity. Raise slot numbers to 16px tx-2. Leave a 16px gap above the bar, or show only the filled slots.

findings.where: controls strip ('wasd walk  shift jog  e use station  m map')
findings.what: The key-cap pills use a different fill and border from the other panels, and the 14px legend text is too small to read from a couch. The strip floats over the stash prop and its edge collides with the weapon bar.
findings.fix: Set the labels to 16px tx-2 and the key caps to 16px tx-1 on --ui-raised with a 4px radius. Pin the strip 16px above the weapon bar, centred. Fold it to one short line, as the controls order says for raids.

findings.where: station labels (wirt the gambler, shop craft and hire, the mainframe and others)
findings.what: The labels are consistent, but their placement varies. Some sit above the prop ('the mainframe', 'the gamble'), some overlap a wall block ('shop, craft, and hire', 'settings'), and the '6 rewards waiting' badge is a second, smaller plate stacked on 'the mainframe'. They are also about 18px with no focus state, so it is unclear which station is active.
findings.fix: Put every label 16px above its prop at 20px f-cond 600 on a --ui-panel plate with a 4px radius. Put the reward count inside the mainframe plate as a lime '6' chip. Give the nearest station a 2px --acc border.

findings.what: The card is inset about 80px from the left and 48px from the top, while the currency line sits near 32px from the right edge. The margins don't match. The sub-line '0 items in stash · 0 runs' is 14px grey and hard to read.
findings.fix: Inset both top corners 48px from the side and 32px from the top. Raise the sub-line to 16px tx-2 and drop the '0 runs' stat if it adds nothing.

findings.what: The lime 32px+ label with an exclamation mark is a strong hero element, but it sits on a plate that overlaps the pillar behind it and is the only text with an exclamation mark. Together with the lime accent it competes with the lime selection rule.
findings.fix: Keep it as the one lime element and drop the '!'. Set it at 32px f-cond 800 with a 2px --acc border plate, 16px above the teal prop, with no pillar behind it.

v.verdict: The wallet hub screen is more focused than the old raid HUD. The hero lime 'enter raid!' sign reads clearly, but the top-right wallet text floats on the void with no panel, and the scene has many competing glows, a clipped and mis-cased bottom bar, and too many equal labels.

findings.what: '$4,471,337', '98,761 xp' and 'stash $0 bag $0' sit unframed, partly on the dark void and partly on the wall. The three groups have mixed sizes and weights and nothing separates them. The stash/bag text is dim grey on near-black, and the money and xp values compete with the 'enter raid!' sign for first read.
findings.fix: Put them in one --ui-panel chip at 85% opacity with a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius and 16px padding, right-aligned 24px from the screen edge. Show '$4,471,337' at 32px f-cond 700 in tx-1. Show 'xp 98,761' at 16px in tx-2 and 'stash $0 · bag $0' at 16px in tx-2, all in one 1x3 vertical or single-row group with 16px gaps. Keep the chip inside the 5% margin.

findings.where: station name tags (shop, gambler, mainframe, stash, fashion, settings, last pour) and the 'enter raid!' sign
findings.what: All the tags use the same near-black pill, but 'enter raid!' is a larger lime-on-black pill at about 56px. It is the only strong primary action, yet it overlaps the pillars and the teal station and sits tight against the top edge. The other labels are nearly as heavy, so the eye has no clear second step.
findings.fix: Keep 'enter raid!' at 40px f-cond 800 with a 2px lime border on the standard panel fill, and give it 16px padding. Drop the other tags to 16px f-cond 600 in tx-1 with 8px padding. Leave only the nearest station's tag lit and dim the rest to tx-2.

findings.what: This is an explaining sentence in amber with asterisks, set in a smaller type than the other tags. It clutters the 'the last pour' station and breaks the clean-copy rule, and it is the only text on screen in warn colour.
findings.fix: Remove the sentence. If a warning must stay, use a 16px 'beta' tag in --warn inside the station pill and no asterisks.

findings.where: bottom hotbar (x 457-1467, y 953-1066) and controls hint (x 757-1165, y 903-937)
findings.what: The hotbar is a raid-style weapon bar on a hub screen where it adds nothing. Seven of nine slots are dim ghost icons, and the slot numbers are 14px grey and low contrast. The controls strip hovers just above it as a second floating bar, and the two bars together cover the bottom of the room and the fashion station.
findings.fix: Hide the hotbar in the hub, or shrink it to the two owned slots. If kept, make slot numbers 16px tx-2 and slot size 64px, and merge the controls into a single fine-print line at 14px beneath the hub, 16px from the screen edge. Remove the separate keycap strip.

findings.what: The card is at a different left margin (81px) from the right wallet (about 25px) and the hotbar. It uses a different title size and style from the wallet, and its sub-line '0 items in stash · 0 runs' is 14px grey and nearly unreadable. The stash count is also repeated in the wallet text.
findings.fix: Align the card to the same 24px margin and the same top as the wallet chip (y 24). Use a 32px f-cond 700 title and a 16px tx-2 sub-line. Delete 'stash $0' from the wallet or the items count from the card so the figure is shown once.

findings.where: proximity glow circles around every station
findings.what: Every station has a large translucent circle in a different hue, with overlapping circles near the mainframe, stash and fashion. They muddy the floor and make the scene look noisy. They also tint the characters, which weakens the single lime accent.
findings.fix: Draw only one 2px ring in tx-2 at 40% opacity around the station the player is in range of, and remove the rest. If a fill is kept, use a flat 8% white for the active station only.

findings.where: 'keyboard' tag (x 912-1007, y 8-31) and '6 rewards waiting' chip (x 1447-1579, y 82-108)
findings.what: The 'keyboard' pill is a teal-outlined mono chip crammed against the top edge at about 14px. The '6 rewards waiting' chip is 14px and stacks tight over the mainframe tag with no gap, so it reads as a second tag. Both are smaller than the 16px floor.
findings.fix: Move 'keyboard' to the bottom-left footer legend at 14px. Raise '6 rewards waiting' to 16px f-cond with a lime dot, and put 8px between it and 'the mainframe'.

findings.where: station sign edges and key hints
findings.what: The keycaps in the controls strip ('wasd', 'shift', 'e', 'm') are 14px and tightly boxed, and the gap between each key and its verb is about 6px. A single 'e use station' is the only action here, yet it is the same weight as 'm map'.
findings.fix: Use 16px keycaps with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and an 8px gap to the verb. Show 'e' in lime and the other keys in tx-2. Align the strip's left edge to the 24px margin.

v.verdict: The roster fold and the ammo card are better, but the hp bar is still a bare strip, the hotbar still shows five dim silhouettes, and the top-left corner stacks four separate elements.

findings.what: The previous fix was not applied. The bar is a bare green slab with no card and no raised track. The 'hp 100' text sits inside the fill in a different weight, and it is flush against the left and bottom edges. The bar is also the loudest saturated block on screen and competes with the ammo hero number.
findings.fix: Put it in a 4px-radius --ui-panel card with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Place the card 24px from the left and bottom edges. Inside it, use a 20px bar with a --ui-raised track. Set 'hp' as a 16px tx-2 label and '100' as a 20px/700 tx-1 number outside the fill. Turn the fill --warn below 50% and --danger below 25%.

findings.where: top-left stack: 'keyboard' chip, 'pillager 236m' arrow, roster card, and the 'pillager' tag with its green bar
findings.what: Four unrelated elements are scattered down the left edge with different widths and styles, and nothing aligns. The 'pillager 236m' label overlaps the arrow. The 'pillager' tag with a bar is orphaned directly under the roster, and it duplicates the hp bar.
findings.fix: Anchor everything to one 24px left margin. Draw the roster at a fixed 360px wide. Leave 16px between the roster, the tag and the chip. Move the 236m direction arrow to the screen edge, away from the 'keyboard' chip. Delete the duplicate tag bar, or merge it into the hp card.

findings.what: The fold line '0 out · 2 dead' is now shown, but the card is open by default. The dead rows still carry a '- dead' column, and 'dead' is repeated twice. The header is 16px and the rows are about 15px, so the card reads small and cramped. The count '1' next to the header is unexplained. Money is right-aligned at a different baseline from the status text.
findings.fix: Fold it by default to the single line '0 out · 2 dead' with the chevron. When open, use 16px/600 rows on a 24px pitch, put dead rows at 40% opacity, and delete the '- dead' text. Align the money column to one right edge with tabular numerals.

findings.what: Five empty slots still show full weapon silhouettes. They are almost the same brightness as the owned weapons, so the owned pistol and rifle carry little emphasis. The tiny slot numbers (about 11px) sit in the corners. The slot 2 'f' chip is unexplained.
findings.fix: Remove the silhouettes from empty slots. Show only a 16px tx-2 number with a 1px --ui-line border at 50% opacity. Keep the 2px lime border on the active slot only. Give the owned rifle in slot 4 a --ui-line-hi border instead of a blue fill. Make the slot numbers 16px.

findings.what: The hero '12 / 24' is good, but the footer 'b / i backpack' and '3 items $1,220' are about 14px and low contrast on the dark card. They are crowded against the bottom edge with no divider. 'b / i' is not a key chip like 'f1'.
findings.fix: Set the footer in 16px/600 f-cond. Add a 1px --ui-line divider above it and 16px card padding. Colour '$1,220' tx-1 and keep '3 items' in tx-2. Draw 'b / i' as a key chip like 'f1'.

findings.what: The timer floats directly on the busy map with only a thin shadow and low separation. The teal chip and its arrow are loose, and the arrow sits detached under the chip. Between the two, the eye lands on the bulwark name plates first.
findings.fix: Put the timer and the chip on one 80% --scrim plate with 8px padding. Set '8:55' at 32px/700. Attach the arrow to the plate's bottom edge with a 4px gap, in --extract.

findings.what: 'contracts 0/8' sits in a box that is both dark and low contrast. Its chevron is detached, and the box is a different width and radius from the roster card. The 'f1 controls' hint is small and floats mid-bottom with no plate, and it is cut off from the hotbar.
findings.fix: Use the same 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border and --ui-panel fill as the roster. Set text at 16px/600. Put 'f1 controls' on a --ui-panel plate with 8px padding, 16px above the hotbar's top edge and left-aligned to it.

findings.where: bulwark name plates 'bulwark b-94' and 'bulwark x-75'
findings.what: The enemy names are about 40px, larger than every other label and the same size as the ammo hero number. They are the first thing the eye hits, over the player and the threat. The plates are oversized, and the orange health bars are thin and hard to read.
findings.fix: Reduce the name to 20px/600 on a --scrim plate with 8px padding. Make the health bar 6px high with a --ui-raised track. Reserve 32px or more for the title and hero number.

v.verdict: The raid screen has a good ammo hero and a calm map. The HUD around it is a patchwork: the top-left panel, the full-width hp bar and the lilac zone name all use different type, fills and margins.

findings.what: A saturated mint green bar with a large 'hp 100' in a font unlike the other HUD text. It sits 24px from the left edge and 12px from the bottom, outside the 5% margin. It is the loudest element on screen but does not match the dark ammo card on the right.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel card (1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius) 48px from the left and bottom edges. Use a 6px bar at --ok, or --danger below 30%. Show '100' at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1 and the 'hp' label at 16px tx-2, so it mirrors the ammo card.

findings.what: Cramped and unclear. The title wording is odd and the bots count '0' is meaningless. Rows are 14-15px with dim tx-2 names and right-aligned prices. The 'you' row is not clearly the hero. The panel hugs the screen edge at 8px. 'dead' sits beside the price, and the chevron is tiny.
findings.fix: Retitle it 'raiders' at 16px f-cond 600 tx-2, with no count. Use 16px rows with 8px padding. Make the 'you' row tx-1 with a lime 3px left bar. Show dead rows in --danger for 'dead' only. Move the panel to the 48px margin and align it with the hp card. Drop the '0 out · 3 dead' footer, or fold it into the title.

findings.what: Two teal pills are stacked, 'extract 146m' and 'extraction c available'. They are redundant and the second reads as an alert with a typo-like glyph. The tiny arrow between them is noise. The 8:56 timer is about 28px, so it is not the hero number.
findings.fix: Merge them into one line: 'extract c · 146m' in a single --extract chip at 20px f-cond 600. Raise the timer to 56px f-cond 800 tx-1 and turn it --danger under 60s. Delete the arrow and the second pill.

findings.what: Nine slots show only two used. Seven dimmed weapon silhouettes add clutter, and they invite readers to think the guns are available. The bar is 1010px wide and crowds the hp bar and ammo card at the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots, at 64px, with the number at 16px tx-2. Give the active slot a 2px lime border. Centre the bar 32px above the bottom edge.

findings.where: zone name 'the long dock cache' (x 1648-1819, y 102-124)
findings.what: Floating lilac text with no panel. The colour is off-palette, since lilac is not in the token list and nearly matches --r-elite. It sits unanchored under the contracts bar.
findings.fix: Use 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 inside the contracts chip, or as a 16px tx-2 line directly under the timer. Remove the lilac.

findings.what: A dark bar with a chevron that sits 17px from the right edge, out of line with the ammo card's edge at 1912. Its 16px text is bold white against a quiet HUD and competes with the timer.
findings.fix: Align it to the same 48px right margin as the ammo card. Make the label 16px tx-2 and the '0/8' tx-1. Use the standard panel fill.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' hint (x 437-538, y 931-955) and 'keyboard' tag (x 8-105, y 5-32)
findings.what: Both are small, floating and unaligned with the other HUD corners. The F1 key chip is a different shape from the hotbar slots, and the green outline on 'keyboard' is a stray accent.
findings.fix: Set both at 14px tx-2 on a --ui-panel chip. Put 'f1 controls' mid-bottom left at the 48px margin. Remove the green outline from 'keyboard'.

findings.where: player nameplates (x 357-406, y 465-487 and x 14-170, y 325-360)
findings.what: 'pillager' is drawn twice, as a nameplate over the head and as a bar at the left. The left bar's thin green line has a third green and duplicates the hp bar. The left card has no clear purpose.
findings.fix: Keep the nameplate over the head and delete the left 'pillager' card. If it stays as the squad row, move it into the raiders panel with a P1 amber marker.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is much quieter: the currency line, the experimental tag, the glow discs and the long controls strip are gone. The result is a clear ammo hero and a one-line controls hint. The bottom-left stack and the bottom edge are still crowded, and the weapon bar is oversized and dim.

findings.where: bottom-left stack (armour 60 bar, hp 100 bar, 'the forge' label)
findings.what: The bars are flat full-width fills with the text jammed into them. The hp bar is clipped by the screen bottom, and 'the forge' floats loose, overlapping the hp bar's top edge in amber. The armour bar uses a bright blue and hp a light green, so both look like template progress bars. hp is a primary survival stat but it sits below armour, with no hierarchy.
findings.fix: Put both bars in one --ui-panel card (4px radius) at x=48, with its bottom 32px above the screen edge. Make hp 24px tall and armour 12px, 8px apart. Use 16px f-cond labels, tx-1, left-aligned, 8px inside the card. Show the hp number at 32px. Use --ok for hp and --r-rare for armour at 90% saturation. Move 'the forge' out of the stack to the world-label layer with an 8px gap, or drop it.

findings.what: The nine empty and idle slots are heavy dark tiles with large weapon silhouettes. They draw as much attention as the active slot. Slot 2 (amber border) and slot 6 (blue fill, 'f' badge) both read as selected, with no single lime focus. The bar touches the bottom edge, and the 'f1 controls' chip is 4px from it.
findings.fix: Draw only the active slot with a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill. Give the others a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 40% opacity and silhouettes at 25% opacity. Mark slot 6 as 'equipped' with a 3px rarity bar instead of a fill. Raise the slot numbers to 16px tx-2 and lift the bar so its bottom is 32px above the screen edge. Put the 'f1 controls' chip 16px above the bar's left end.

findings.what: '0 sp' at 56px is the right hero. But 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' are about 14px and read as dim grey on black. The timer '9:56' sits at the card's lower edge, and the 'extract 117m' chip hangs half outside the card on a different fill. Together they make two stacked boxes with mismatched edges.
findings.fix: Merge them into one card, 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px padding. Row 1: 'team score' at 16px tx-2. Row 2: '0 sp' at 56px 800 tx-1, with 'you' and 'p2' at 16px tx-2 on the right in amber and cyan. Row 3: the timer at 32px, with 'extract 117m' at 16px --extract on the same row, right-aligned. Make all text at least 4.5:1.

findings.what: The two corner widgets use different fills, border radii and type sizes. The 'keyboard' badge is a tiny 16px tag in lime-green monospace-looking text, which breaks the Barlow-only rule. The goals box is a 32px bold label with a chevron, which is oversized for its importance. Neither aligns with the 48px margin.
findings.fix: Use the same card style for both: --ui-panel, 4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 48px from the screen edge and 32px from the top. Set both labels to 16px f-cond 600. Set 'keyboard' in tx-2, not lime, since lime means selected. Shrink 'goals 0/3' to 20px with a 16px chevron.

findings.what: The hero number '30 / 180' is good. But the card is 270px wide and sits tight against the right and bottom edges (about 8px), which breaks the 48px margin. 'compact smg' at 28px competes with the title tier. The slash and the reserve value are the same weight as the loaded count.
findings.fix: Move the card so it sits 48px from the right edge and 32px from the bottom. Set 'compact smg' to 20px tx-2. Keep '30' at 56px 800 tx-1 and set '/ 180' to 20px tx-2. Align the card's bottom edge with the weapon bar's bottom.

findings.where: player 2 tag, top-left (and the in-world 'player 2' label)
findings.what: The left-edge tag has a thin cyan bar on a dark blue plate, and its text is bright blue. The in-world label uses a different plate and size. The shield label overlaps the P1 character, and 'shield' is clipped by the bubble.
findings.fix: Make both labels use one style: 16px f-cond cyan on --ui-panel at 80%, 4px radius, 8px padding. Put the P2 tag at x=48, y=32 below the keyboard tag, 8px gap. Move the 'shield' label 8px below the character and clear of the ring.

v.verdict: The hp and armour bars are now clearly built and the top-centre alerts are tidier, but the HUD still mixes unrelated styles, with a capital-letter violation, floating unboxed elements and a stacked score card that crowds the centre.

findings.where: top-left 'keyboard' tag (x 10-105, y 6-32) and 'player 1' plate (x 16-170, y 325-360)
findings.what: The 'keyboard' tag is a green-outlined bold chip, a style used nowhere else. The 'player 1' plate floats mid-left with no relation to the hp card and no corner anchor. P1 should be amber, but it reads cyan/teal, and a second 'player 1' label sits over the character. The same name is drawn three times.
findings.fix: Delete the mid-left plate. Keep only the over-head label, 16px f-cond 600, in P1 amber. Fold 'keyboard' into the hp card as a 14px tx-2 device tag, or drop it. Anchor all player info in one card at the 48px margin.

findings.where: hp and armour bars bottom-left (x 24-430, y 968-1068)
findings.what: The bars are the wrong weight for the HUD. The hp bar is a saturated 34px slab with 'hp 100' at about 32px bold, while the armour bar is a flat blue pill, so the two share no style. Both sit 24px from the edge, not on the 48px margin, and the hp bar touches the bottom edge. Nothing here matches the ammo card's panel treatment on the right, and the hp bar's fill and label have weak contrast.
findings.fix: Put both in one --ui-panel card (1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius) 48px from the left and bottom, bottom-aligned with the ammo card (y 1032). Make the bars 8px tall, with hp in --ok and armour in a blue-grey. Show labels at 16px tx-2 and '100' at 32px f-cond 700 tx-1.

findings.where: top-centre score card (x 810-1112, y 0-107) with the extract pill (x 889-1033, y 102-133)
findings.what: The card is flush against the top edge, with 'team score', '0 sp', 'you 0 sp', 'pl 0 sp' and the timer packed in at four or five different sizes. The extract pill is jammed onto its bottom border and overlaps it, and the teal arrow floats below the pill with no container. It is crowded, and the hero number competes with the alert below.
findings.fix: Offset the card 16px from the top. Use one hero: the timer '9:57' at 56px f-cond 800. Make 'team score 0 sp' a 20px row and the per-player scores 16px tx-2. Merge the pill and the arrow into one extract chip at 20px --extract, 16px below the card, with an 8px gap to the arrow.

findings.what: This is the loudest element on screen: a 40px red bold banner with a warning glyph, plus a red edge bar. It sits right under the extract pill and covers the wall behind it, so it fights the hero number and pulls the eye away from play. The two-tone red fill reads as a generic alert template.
findings.fix: Shrink the text to 20px f-cond 700 in tx-1 on a --ui-panel strip with a 3px --danger left bar and a 4px radius. Keep it centred, 24px under the extract chip, with 16px padding. Fade it out after 2s.

findings.what: All nine slots are drawn even though only two are owned, so seven dark empty slots with ghost weapon silhouettes take up the centre bottom. The active slot's yellow border is thin and similar in tone to the 'f' badge and rarity bars. The slot numbers are about 14px and dim, and the bar sits just 18px from the bottom edge, 6px off the controls label.
findings.fix: Show only owned slots (2 here) at 64px, with the number at 16px tx-2. Give the active slot a 2px --acc border and --ui-raised fill. Lift the bar to 32px above the bottom edge. Drop the silhouettes.

findings.where: 'goals 0/3' dropdown top-right (x 1605-1903, y 22-65) and 'the forge' label (x 1684-1760, y 255-275)
findings.what: The goals box is a bright-bordered dropdown with a chevron and a 24px label, which makes it the one chunky box in the corner, with no panel match to the other cards and no pad focus. The forge label is amber 20px text floating over art with no backing, so it has weak contrast on the dusk tint.
findings.fix: Restyle goals as a 16px f-cond 600 header on a --ui-panel card (1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius) at the 48px margin, with a 14px tx-2 count. Give the forge label a 16px tx-1 text shadow, or an 8px-padded --ui-panel chip with a --warn glyph.

findings.what: The hint is a small dark chip right against the hotbar edge (6px away) at about 18px, so it reads as part of the hotbar. The 'f1' key cap doesn't match the other key hints, and the chip has no clear anchor to the left margin.
findings.fix: Put it at x 48 on the same baseline as the hp card top, 16px f-cond 600 tx-2, with a 1px --ui-line-hi key cap around 'f1'. Keep at least 24px clear of the hotbar.

findings.what: The card is the best-built element but still off the system. It sits 8px from the right edge, not 48px, and it floats 60px above the bottom, so it is not aligned with the hp card. '25 / 150' has two weights and sizes of the same number, and the 'auto rifle' label is right-aligned at about 28px, close to the hero size.
findings.fix: Move it to the 48px margin and bottom-align it with the hp card at y 1032. Make '25' 56px f-cond 800 and '/ 150' 20px tx-2. Set 'auto rifle' to 16px f-cond 600 tx-2, left-aligned.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is readable and mostly consistent. The ammo hero number works and the bottom hotbar is tidy. The left list is cramped, there are too many different type sizes and weights, and the hp and stamina bars look unfinished.

findings.what: The hp bar is a flat bright green fill with oversized 'hp 100' text that is cramped inside it. The stamina bar is a dim blue-grey with low-contrast text, so the two bars don't match in size, weight or style. They float at the screen edge with no panel and no relation to the hotbar or the ammo card. This is the most important survival readout, yet it looks like a placeholder.
findings.fix: Put both bars in one --ui-panel card with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, aligned to the hotbar's baseline and 24px from the screen edge. Make both bars 20px tall. Use a 16px f-cond label left-aligned inside each bar, with the value right-aligned in --tx-1. Use --ok for hp and a muted --extract for stamina. Drop the 100% saturated green.

findings.what: The panel is a dense 9-row text block at about 14-16px, with mixed colours (purple name, white, grey) and a '- dead' column of identical rows. The title reads as a bold header but carries a meaningless '0'. The footer line '0 out · 7 dead' repeats what the rows already say. It is clutter in the corner that has the least importance, and it competes with the minimap.
findings.fix: Collapse it to one line by default, such as 'bots 0 out · 7 dead', and open the list only on a key. If it stays, use a 16px minimum, drop the '- dead' repeats, show only the survivors, and remove the '0' from the title. Set the rows in --tx-2, with --tx-1 only for 'you'. Give the panel the same 24px margin as the minimap.

findings.what: The minimap is large (about 300px) and mostly empty black, with a lower half that carries no information. Its icons are tiny and illegible, and the collapse caret is 12px. The contracts bar below uses a different header style (bold, no hierarchy) and sits tight against the map with only about 8px of gap. The corner is heavy compared with the quiet centre.
findings.fix: Crop the minimap to a square of about 240px and give it the same 4px radius and border as the other panels. Enlarge the icons to 12px or more. Set the contracts row to 16px --tx-2 with a 16px gap above it. Align the right margin of the minimap, the contracts row and the ammo card to the same 24px.

findings.what: The timer '9:00' is a 40px bold numeral and reads as the hero, but its sunrise icon is a small, murky dark circle. The 'extract 138m' chip is a teal-outlined pill with a tiny arrow under it, which is a third shape language next to the rectangular panels. Both sit over a busy building edge, with no backing for the timer.
findings.fix: Put the timer and the extract chip in one 4px-radius --ui-panel card, centred, with a 1px --extract border only on the extract row. Make the icon 24px with a clear glyph. Drop the pill radius and keep the arrow inside the card.

findings.where: prompt below the player, 'empty slot · [lb] [rb] gun'
findings.what: The tooltip is a black pill with 20px bold text and bracketed key hints, set over a yellow 'p1' tag. The two stack tightly with no gap, and the bracket glyphs are not the pad button icons used elsewhere. It reads as a debug string, and it is explaining text on screen.
findings.fix: Shorten it to 'empty slot' with LB and RB shown as 16px key chips. Use a 4px radius to match the other panels. Leave 8px between it and the p1 tag, and fade it out after 3 seconds.

findings.what: The hotbar is clean overall, but the slot numbers are 12px and low contrast. The empty and inactive weapons are dark silhouettes, so slot 2 (selected, amber outline) and slot 7 (filled amber) use two different highlight treatments. Only slot 7 shows an ammo count. The amber outline on a P1 slot also conflicts with 'lime only means selected'.
findings.fix: Use one selected treatment: a 2px --acc border plus a --ui-raised fill, on the slot that is actually equipped. Set the slot numbers at 16px in --tx-2. Show the ammo count on every loaded slot in 16px, and dim the empty slots to 40% opacity.

findings.what: This card is the strongest element: '5 / 50' is a good hero number, and the weapon name is above it. But the weapon name is 24px, bigger than the 20px body size, and is right-aligned against a left-aligned footer row. The 'view backpack' and '4 items $3,510' labels at 14px are small, and they are not aligned to the bottom edge of the hotbar. The card's top is also 60px taller than the hotbar.
findings.fix: Set the weapon name at 20px in --tx-2, the hero number at 56px, and the footer at 16px. Align the card's bottom edge and height with the hotbar (about 110px). Left-align the name and footer, or right-align both.

findings.what: Edge margins are inconsistent: the left list sits at 8px, the hp bar at 22px, the minimap at 18px, and the ammo card at 20px. The panels also use different borders and fills, with some translucent and some opaque, so the HUD does not read as one system.
findings.fix: Use a 24px safe margin for all four corners. Use one panel style for everything: --ui-panel at 85% opacity, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius.

v.verdict: A readable raid HUD with a clear ammo hero number and a clean hotbar, but the hotbar's selection state is confusing, the left roster is dense, and type sizes and colours drift from the style guide.

findings.what: Two slots are highlighted at once. Slot 2 has an amber border but is dimmed, and slot 7 has a gold fill and holds the live weapon. Players can't tell which slot is selected, and amber is used where lime is meant to mean 'selected'. The tooltip 'empty slot' also sits away from the slot it describes.
findings.fix: Use one selected state: a 2px --acc border plus --ui-raised fill on the active slot only. Make the border on every other slot 1px --ui-line-hi. If slot 2 is the cursor and slot 7 is the equipped weapon, give the equipped weapon a separate small marker instead of a second highlight. Anchor the tooltip directly above its slot.

findings.what: A 7-row dead list takes about 360x190px of prime screen space. The grey and purple names are 14-15px with weak contrast. The panel is a hard-edged box with a chevron. 'dead' repeated 7 times is noise, and two lines ('0 out · 7 dead') say the same thing. The purple name has no legend.
findings.fix: Collapse the dead rows to a single summary line ('0 out · 7 dead'). Show only the live pillagers, at --fs-label 16px in --tx-2. Drop the purple highlight or explain it. Use a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius.

findings.what: The '9:00' is about 28px, but the guide wants a hero-sized number (56px) for the extract timer. The 'extract 136m' teal pill is small (about 16px) and sits tight under the clock with a stray teal arrow beneath it. The clock icon in an amber circle competes with the number.
findings.fix: Make the extract distance the hero element at 40-56px --f-cond 800 in --extract teal. Shrink the clock to a --fs-label tag. Keep the icon as a 16px glyph with no filled circle. Drop the arrow or move it into the pill.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' text is bigger and bolder than the 'stamina' label. Both bars hug the screen edge at x=24 and y=1045, inside the 5% margin. The stamina text is on a blue fill with poor contrast. The two bars' gap and heights don't match the hotbar's baseline.
findings.fix: Inset the bars to the 5% margin (about 54px left, 54px bottom). Set both labels at 16px --f-cond 600 in --tx-1 with the value right-aligned. Make both bars 20px tall with an 8px gap. Align the bottom edge to the hotbar's bottom (y≈1060).

findings.what: '5 / 50' is a strong hero number, but the card is jammed to the corner, about 10px from the screen edge. 'view backpack' at about 14px and '4 items $3,510' are too small and dim for a couch. The weapon name 'longshot' is right-aligned while the footer text is split left and right.
findings.fix: Inset the card to the 5% margin. Set 'view backpack' and the item line at 16px in --tx-2. Align the weapon name with the number's right edge, and keep one left or right axis per row.

findings.what: The minimap is a near-black box with sparse, hard-to-read blocks and tiny icons about 10px. The contracts bar is another separate box with a chevron, so this corner has two boxes with different corner treatments and weights. It also sits tight to the screen edge.
findings.fix: Join the minimap and contracts into one --ui-panel card with a single 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Put the contracts row under the minimap as a 16px label with a 1px --ui-line divider. Enlarge the map icons to at least 14px and inset the card to the margin.

findings.what: The tooltip is a free-floating black pill in the middle of the playfield, with bold white text at about 20px. It looks heavier than the HUD panels and its bracket key hints are inline in the sentence.
findings.fix: Reuse the panel style (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius). Move it to sit just above its slot. Render the key hints as small 16px key-cap glyphs and drop the dot separator.

findings.what: Panels use inconsistent treatments: the roster has a thin light border, the contracts card has a rounded bar, the weapon card has a darker fill, and the hotbar slots have a different radius. Icons and pills differ in border colour, so the HUD reads as separate widgets rather than one system.
findings.fix: Apply the one panel recipe (--ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding) to every HUD block. Keep accent colours for state only (--acc selected, --extract teal for extraction).

v.verdict: The raid HUD is readable and mostly flat and dark, but it carries capitals, three competing slot highlights, a bar that's missing its text, and a cluttered top-left list, so it doesn't yet read as one coherent system.

findings.where: hotbar slot 2 vs slot 7, and the 'p2' tag
findings.what: Slot 2 (empty) has the same bright gold/lime outline as slot 7 (the equipped gun), so two slots read as selected. Slot 2's outline competes with the real equipped weapon. The 'p2' tag is also cyan with a box, and the 'empty slot · [lb] [rb] gun' tooltip below it is another competing callout.
findings.fix: Give lime a single meaning (selected). Slot 2 gets a --ui-line-hi 1px border with a dimmed icon. Slot 7 gets a 2px --acc border plus an --ui-raised fill. Drop the ownership tag to 14px, or fold it into the tooltip.

findings.what: An 8-row list with a 'dead' column, a purple name and a '0 out · 7 dead' footer. It sits in the corner above the action and explains rather than informs. The purple name introduces an off-palette colour. Most rows are dim grey at about 14px, below the readable floor.
findings.fix: Collapse to a single line, '7 dead · 0 out', at 16px tx-2 and expand on a key. If the list stays, use 16px tx-1 names, drop 'dead' from every row, remove the purple, and fix the row height to 24px.

findings.what: The stamina bar is a washed blue-grey with 'stamina' as text, and the hp bar is a flat green with a very large 'hp 100'. Their type sizes differ (about 20px vs about 32px), so the bars have no shared structure. The hp text is crowded against the bar's left edge, and the green fill against the lime accent weakens the 'lime = selected' rule.
findings.fix: Make both bars 12px tall with the same width. Put a 16px label above each in tx-2. Give hp the one hero number, in tx-1 at 32px, right-aligned. Use --ok for hp, and tx-2 at 40% for stamina. Align the left edge to the 5% margin (96px).

findings.what: The '5 / 50' ammo number is the strongest hero element, but 'longshot 4x scope' is long and carries a spec. 'view backpack' and '4 items $3,510' sit at about 14px, which is too small. The money line repeats the '$3,510' shown top-left in the bot list.
findings.fix: Use 'longshot' alone at 20px. Move the 4x label to a 16px tag. Set 'view backpack' and the item count at 16px tx-2. Remove the duplicate $3,510 from one location.

findings.where: contract item toast, bottom-left of centre
findings.what: The orange left-bar toast reads 'contract Item nearby · gold glow marks the box'. It has a capital 'I', which breaks the all-lower-case rule, and it's an explaining sentence. The 13px grey detail text is below the floor.
findings.fix: Make it 'contract item nearby' in lower case at 16px, and drop the explaining clause. Use --warn only for the glyph and keep the text tx-1.

findings.where: keyboard tag, top-left; minimap and contracts
findings.what: The 'keyboard' tag is a green pill in a different style from every other panel (border colour, radius, weight). The 'contracts 0/8' bar and minimap use another border treatment, and the minimap map content is cluttered with tiny icons.
findings.fix: Use one panel style everywhere (--ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius, 16px/600 label). Restyle the keyboard tag to match, and drop the minimap icons to 3 or fewer types.

findings.what: '9:00' at about 28px, with an 'extract 139m' pill and a pointer triangle, is a good start. But the teal pill and the tiny amber icon next to the time add colours, and the 139m is 16px.
findings.fix: Raise the timer to the 56px hero size only if it is the screen's one hero (otherwise ammo is). Pick one, and keep the other at 32px. Make the sun icon tx-2.

findings.what: Empty slots show dimmed gun silhouettes at nearly the same weight as the real item, so 'empty' versus 'owned' is hard to read. The key numbers (1–0) are 12px and low-contrast.
findings.fix: Draw empty slots with only the number, 16px tx-2, and no silhouette. Draw owned weapons at full opacity. Set the slot to 96px wide with 8px gaps, with rarity bars 3px.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD is readable and mostly all lower case, with a decent hero ammo number, but it breaks the guide in several places: three different corner panel styles, a 'p2' tag that is the wrong colour, small type, and a hint that explains itself.

findings.where: top-left pillager-bots list and the top-right minimap/contracts card
findings.what: The two corner panels do not match each other or the bottom-right ammo card. The bots list has a hard 1px light border and tight rows, the minimap is a different dark box with a chevron, and the ammo card is a third style. Corner radii and fills vary. The bots list is also long: 8 rows plus a footer for information the player rarely needs.
findings.fix: Use one panel: fill #16191b, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Collapse the bots list to one line by default ('7 dead · 0 out') and open it with a key. Give the minimap and contracts header the same header row height (32px).

findings.what: Row text is about 14px, with grey names on a translucent dark panel over a busy green map. This is under the 16px floor for anything read, and the repeated '- dead' column adds noise. One name (fbi_surveillance_van) is purple with no explanation, which breaks the rule that colour carries meaning.
findings.fix: Set names to 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Drop '- dead' from each row and show only the count. Give the panel a solid 0.92 fill. Remove the purple tint, or limit it to the rarity palette.

findings.what: The tag is a small teal-filled box with a cyan border. Teal is reserved for extraction, and P2 is cyan per the guide, so the two colours are confusable. The tag is tiny, about 16px, and low in contrast against the tan ground.
findings.fix: Use the exact P2 cyan from the ring and tag. Make the text 16px with 8px/4px padding on a --ui-panel fill, and keep teal for extraction. The 'extract 137m' pill uses the same teal, so make the two clearly different.

findings.what: This is an explaining sentence on screen that also floats in the middle of the play area. It shows the key hint with brackets and a middle dot, while the other HUD cards use different hint styles. The player does not need to be told a slot is empty.
findings.fix: Remove the sentence. Show only a key-hint chip ('lb rb') in 16px --tx-2 inside the empty slot, or show it only while that slot is focused. If it stays, use the same panel as the other cards, 16px, with 8px padding.

findings.what: Nine slots of equal weight, with silhouettes that are nearly invisible at 1080 on a couch. Slot 2 is highlighted gold/amber while slot 7 is the real active gun with a gold-ish border too, so it is unclear which one is selected. Amber and gold also compete with the lime accent. Slot numbers are about 12px.
findings.fix: Show one selected state only, with a 2px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill, and dim every other slot to 40%. Raise the slot numbers to 16px. Use the lime accent for selection, not amber or gold. Brighten the idle icons to --tx-2.

findings.what: The hp bar is a bright flat green with a large 'hp 100' label in a different type treatment from the stamina label. The stamina label sits on a blue bar at about 20px and the hp label at about 32px with different baselines. The bars are not aligned to the 5% margin and sit hard against the screen edge at x=23.
findings.fix: Use one label size (20px f-cond 600) on both bars, with hp as the hero number only if it is the one thing on this screen at 56px. Inset the bars 48px from the left and bottom edges. Match the bar height to 24px for both and use the --ok token for hp.

findings.what: The hero '5 / 50' is good, but the card also holds 'view backpack' and '4 items $3,510' at about 14px, which is the minimum. The card edge nearly touches the right screen edge, and the contrast of the grey text is weak. The $3,510 shown here duplicates the same figure in the bots list.
findings.fix: Keep the hero at 56px and drop the footer row, or set it to 16px in --tx-2. Show the stash value in one place only. Add a 48px margin to the right and bottom edges.

findings.where: top-centre timer and the 'keyboard' badge at the top-left
findings.what: '9:00' is a 30px number with a small sun icon, and below it a teal 'extract 137m' pill and an arrow. The timer reads as heavy and the pill is small. The 'keyboard' badge in the top-left corner uses a bordered green style seen nowhere else, and it is not aligned to the margin.
findings.fix: Set the timer to 32px and the pill label to 16px with the extract teal reserved for the pill. Restyle the 'keyboard' badge as a --ui-panel chip with a 1px #4a5257 border, 16px text, and put it at the 48px margin or remove it from the raid HUD.

v.verdict: The empty-slot prompt is gone and the bars are cleaner, but the open controls list is now the largest panel on screen and the bots list, minimap and bars still ignore the margin and type scale.

findings.what: The raid-controls list is a 355x265px block of 13px-ish text with 'move / fight / gear' labels. It is the biggest panel on screen, sits on top of the play area, and is open in a career-style view where it should be folded. The text is dim and below the 16px minimum, and the two columns are uneven (left 11 rows, right 6).
findings.fix: Fold it to one 16px line at mid-bottom left ('f1 controls'), and open it only on F1. If it stays open for the party demo, set the text to 16px --tx-1 with the key chips in --ui-line-hi, and balance it to 8 rows per column.

findings.what: The bars are unchanged and are not in a card. hp is a saturated flat green with a 40px 'hp 100' in the display font. Stamina is a washed grey-blue with 20px dim text at low contrast. Their left edge (22px) matches neither the bots panel (8px) nor the controls panel (16px), and the hp label is bolder than the hero ammo number, so two things compete for 'hero'.
findings.fix: Put both bars in one --ui-panel card with a 4px radius and a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 24px from the edges and bottom-aligned with the hotbar. Make the bars 16px tall with a 16px f-cond label on the left and the value on the right in --tx-1. Use --ok for hp, and desaturate stamina to a muted --extract.

findings.what: The list is a 360px panel at 8px from the edge with 16px text in tight 18px rows. The title 'current pillager bots 7' is the same weight as the rows.
